Though dressed in vivid red and bearing little affection for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew, Gilthares is not picky about who aids his breakout—so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

npc:gnoarn.text: Gnoarn. Gnoarn is an exiled gnome residing in Tinker Town within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Displaced following the devastating fall of Gnomeregan, he assists his scattered people by directing adventurers to assist fellow gnomish engineers and survivors. Like the majority of his brethren, Gnoarn was forced to flee the depths of Gnomeregan when troggs invaded and catastrophic radiation rendered the great subterranean metropolis uninhabitable. Taking refuge in Ironforge's Tinker Town under the hospitality of the Bronzebeard dwarves, Gnoarn spends his days keeping track of other survivors. He serves as an informal coordinator among the refugees, pointing capable travelers toward gnomes abroad who urgently require assistance, such as the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan or the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

npc:godrick-farsan.text: Godrick Farsan. Godrick Farsan is an undead warlock assistant located in the Undercity, serving alongside Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter. Despite being entirely blind, he says that he sees in a different way. Situated amidst the summoning circles of the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Master Carendin Halgar in guiding aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Though he lacks physical sight, Godrick says he can still see in a different way, without explaining the means. He tests practitioners seeking to bind greater demonic entities, dispatching them to gather pure hearts and essences needed for intricate summoning rituals.

npc:golnir-bouldertoe.text: Golnir Bouldertoe. Golnir Bouldertoe is a dwarven mining vendor stationed beside the bustling Great Forge in Ironforge. He provides essential supplies for miners and prospectors while handling dispatches for local couriers and travelers. Standing within the roaring heat of Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen with the necessities of their trade. From sturdy mining picks to fluxes and coal, his wares fuel the tireless smelting fires and smithies that define the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a reliable point of contact for workers arriving in the city, often directing fresh hands or receiving supply missives shuttled in from nearby outposts.

npc:gorbold-steelhand.text: Gorbold Steelhand. Gorbold Steelhand is a dwarven merchant stationed in Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore. Operating far from the snowy halls of Khaz Modan, he supplies travelers, crafters, and local night elves with general goods and trade supplies. While most of Kalimdor's northern reaches are populated by the secretive night elves, Alliance outposts like Auberdine rely on merchants from across the Great Sea to keep trade moving. Gorbold Steelhand represents the far-reaching presence of Ironforge commerce in the region. Working alongside the kaldorei, he sells trade goods, reagents, crafting sundries, and tools to adventurers preparing to explore the treacherous shores and forests of Darkshore. Beyond stocking daily goods, Gorbold keeps a keen eye on the perilous coastal waters off Auberdine. Darkshore's reef-strewn waters are notorious for swallowing Alliance vessels, and merchants like Gorbold have a direct interest in the cargo lost beneath the waves. Travelers willing to dive into the deep ocean can often find him interested in the salvage and lost logs scattered across sunken wrecks.

npc:gordon-wendham.text: Gordon Wendham. Gordon Wendham is a Forsaken weaponsmith and merchant operating out of the bustling Trade Quarter in the Undercity. He equips newly arrived champions and local defenders of the Dark Lady with reliable steel, blades, and bludgeons. Beyond hawking basic armaments, he frequently serves as a local point of contact for couriers arriving from the surface. Situated amidst the damp stonework and chemical canals of the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham provides essential weaponry to those taking up arms for the Forsaken. From basic daggers and hand axes to sturdy broadswords and maces, his stock caters to fledgling fighters who need dependable iron before venturing out into the contested reaches of Lordaeron. Beyond his merchant trade, Wendham is integrated into the capital's busy logistics network. Travelers sent on errands from flight masters and couriers—such as those connecting from the bat handlers atop the ruins—are often directed straight to his stall. His central location in the Trade Quarter makes him an accessible and recognizable fixture for coordinating basic supplies and dispatches throughout the underground city.

npc:gramma-stonefield.text: Gramma Stonefield. Gramma Stonefield, whose given name is Mildred, is the elderly matriarch of the Stonefield family residing at their farm in Elwynn Forest. Unlike her bickering kin, she has grown weary of the bitter, generations-long feud with the neighboring Maclures. Quietly working behind her family's back, she does everything she can to help her grandson Tommy Joe pursue his forbidden romance with Maybell Maclure. As the oldest living member of the Stonefield clan, Mildred Stonefield has witnessed decades of petty squabbling between her household and the Maclures across the road. Rather than stoking the bad blood, she views the enduring rivalry as senseless and destructive. When her grandson Tommy Joe Stonefield falls in love with Maybell Maclure, Gramma chooses compassion over clan loyalty. Relying on an old friendship with William Pestle in Goldshire, she quietly plots to help the star-crossed sweethearts meet in secret, subverting the stubborn hostility dividing the two farms.

npc:grand-mason-marblesten.text: Grand Mason Marblesten. Grand Mason Marblesten is an esteemed dwarven stonemason stationed in the busy Commons of Ironforge. Deeply devoted to the royal legacy of Khaz Modan, he has been commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard to build a memorial to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. Adventurers often meet him when assisting with the materials needed to complete this solemn tribute. Dwarven stonemasonry is not merely a trade; it is an enduring art form that shapes the very soul of Ironforge. Grand Mason Marblesten stands among the city's foremost masters of the chisel, representing the centuries-old tradition of carving halls, pillars, and great effigies straight from the living mountain. Based in the Commons, he oversees civic projects and commemorative monuments that immortalize Bronzebeard history. Marblesten's most poignant task is a memorial King Magni commissioned for Sully Balloo, a soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy, as a tribute to his grieving widow. Wanting a truly lasting piece, the Grand Mason insists on one of the finest stones available: Alterac Granite from Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad.

npc:granis-swiftaxe.text: Granis Swiftaxe. Granis Swiftaxe is a dwarf warrior trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Known for his blunt demeanor and hardy training regimen, he mentors fledgling Alliance fighters emerging from Coldridge Pass before directing seasoned warriors to the city of Ironforge. Found warming himself among the casks of the Thunderbrew Distillery, Granis Swiftaxe serves as the primary combat instructor for young warriors traversing Dun Morogh. He possesses the unyielding pride typical of dwarven fighters, showing open amusement and disdain toward non-warriors who try to catch his ear. Once a student demonstrates sufficient prowess in combat, Granis sends them up the mountain path to seek out master trainer Muren Stormpike in the Military Ward of Ironforge.

npc:great-father-winter.text: Great-father Winter. Great-father Winter is an elderly orc hired by the Smokywood Pastures merchant company to pose as the legendary holiday figure in Orgrimmar. Stationed near Grommash Hold in the Valley of Strength during the Feast of Winter Veil, he listens to children's wishes while visibly growing weary of commercial holiday cheer. In exchange for holiday gifts and seasonal tasks, he routinely asks passersby for gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk. While ancient lore speaks of Greatfather Winter as a majestic, elemental spirit wandering the land bringing snow and seasonal renewal, the figure sitting in the Valley of Strength is rather more mundane. He is an orc performer on the payroll of Smokywood Pastures, hired specifically to drive commerce, promote company wares, and entertain the youth of the Horde. Critics grumble that this commercial mascot cheapens genuine seasonal traditions, but few can deny the festive buzz he brings to the city streets. Stationed right outside Grommash Hold beneath the boughs of decorated evergreens, this stand-in endures an exhausting shift of children clambering onto his lap to state their gift demands. Between corporate plug drops for Smokywood Pastures discounts and half-hearted holiday greetings, his endurance frequently wanes. He openly admits to keeping a bottle of festive spirits stashed in his pack to drown out the noise as soon as his shift finishes, relying heavily on visiting adventurers to deliver snacks to keep him going.

npc:greatfather-winter.text: Greatfather Winter. Greatfather Winter is the legendary personification of the winter season and the central figure of the Feast of Winter Veil. While ancient legends revere him as a mythical being who blankets Azeroth in snow to allow the land to rest and renew, modern city-dwellers know him primarily through the commercial spectacle managed by the goblins of Smokywood Pastures. According to ancient lore, Greatfather Winter is an ethereal wanderer who walks the world late in the year, casting his billowing snowy cloak across the land so nature may slumber and be reborn. Dwarves view him as an embodiment or herald of the titans, pointing to the frosted crags of Dun Morogh as living proof of his favor. Other traditions, such as those of the tauren, respect his role in the season's turning while attributing the cold and storms to the elemental work of the Sun and Moon, giving the Earth Mother time to rest. Wherever the legend traveled, communities learned to gather and feast together against the cold, celebrating the promise of returning life. In major settlements like Ironforge and Orgrimmar, the ancient spirit has been thoroughly reshaped by the enterprising goblins of Smokywood Pastures. The trading cartel popularized the depiction of Greatfather Winter as a jolly, red-suited elder with a white beard who rides a flying sleigh and hands out holiday treats and toys. Smokywood Pastures hires local actors—a dwarf in Ironforge and an orc in Orgrimmar—to listen to children's wishlists, receive offerings of milk and gingerbread cookies, and advertise seasonal merchandise beneath lavishly decorated trees.

npc:greatmother-hawkwind.text: Greatmother Hawkwind. Greatmother Hawkwind is a revered tauren elder resting by the water well on Red Cloud Mesa. As the mother of Camp Narache's leader, Chief Hawkwind, she embodies the enduring spirit and communal responsibility of the tribe despite her advanced age. Greatmother Hawkwind spends her days beside the fresh water well at Camp Narache, serving as the spiritual matriarch for young tauren beginning their rites of passage. Though years have slowed her stride, she refuses to let age sideline her duty to the village. She believes that every member of the tribe, young or old, has an active role to play in sustaining the community, often asking fledgling youths to lend a hand with simple domestic chores like fetching fresh water. As the mother of Chief Hawkwind, the chieftain of Camp Narache, Greatmother Hawkwind provides steady counsel and quiet dignity amidst the threats facing Red Cloud Mesa. While her son organizes hunters and warriors against encroaching Bristleback quilboar and local predators, she tends to the moral heart of the settlement, reminding the newly awakened that strength begins with humility and service to one's kin.

npc:greta-mosshoof.text: Greta Mosshoof. Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid allied with the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary in southern Felwood. Alongside night elves and fellow guardians of nature, she investigates the foul taint creeping across the ancient forest and directs scouts into the Shadow Council stronghold of Jaedenar. Stationed at the Emerald Sanctuary on the southern boundary of Felwood, Greta Mosshoof works alongside the Emerald Circle to combat the pervasive corruption consuming the ancient woods. Rather than surrendering the blighted lands to the demonic taint left in the wake of the Third War, she coordinates efforts to understand and push back the spreading rot. Her investigations zero in on the poisoned waters of Felwood and the foul cultists burrowed within Jaedenar.

npc:grimbooze-thunderbrew.text: Grimbooze Thunderbrew. Grimbooze Thunderbrew is an eccentric dwarven brewer of the Thunderbrew clan, camped out in the Dagger Hills of Westfall. He spends his days concocting potent spirits and speaking almost entirely in verse. Hailing from the renowned Thunderbrew brewing family of Kharanos, Grimbooze left the snowy mountain peaks of Dun Morogh for the windswept hills of Westfall. Known for his jovial disposition and an unyielding passion for potent spirits, he has a peculiar habit of speaking strictly in rhymes, and he answers a traveler's questions only once they have completed a simple task for him. Travelers passing through the dangerous Dagger Hills can find him tending to his private casks, always eager to test a thirsty traveler's palate.

npc:grish-longrunner.text: Grish Longrunner. Grish Longrunner is a tauren scout and messenger stationed near the Great Lift, the vital mechanical crossing connecting the southern Barrens with the canyons of Thousand Needles. Serving the interests of the Horde along this bustling boundary, he keeps watch over travelers and coordinates military movement across the frontier. Positioned right beside the towering machinery of the Great Lift, Grish Longrunner stands watch over one of central Kalimdor's most precarious border crossings. The platform elevator is a lifeline connecting the arid wastes of the southern Barrens to the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles below. Between roving quilboar packs and competing territorial threats, travel along this vertical boundary is dangerous, making scouts like Grish essential for keeping the Horde informed and summoning reinforcements where they are sorely needed.

npc:grub.text: Grub. Grub is an enterprising orc living in a roadside hut just east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Operating a modest frontier eatery alongside a cook and a baker, he is famous—or perhaps notorious—for introducing travelers to the culinary uses of local vermin. Tucked against the crags just east of the Crossroads, Grub oversees a rustic dwelling shared with Duhng, his cook, and Tarban Hearthgrain, a baker. While life on the plains demands a hearty stomach, Grub takes frontier self-sufficiency to an extreme. Rather than letting the abundant dig rats of the Barrens go to waste, he has turned them into a staple ingredient, offering to teach passing wanderers how to simmer the subterranean rodents into a savory, if unglamorous, stew.

npc:grull-hawkwind.text: Grull Hawkwind. Grull Hawkwind is a young tauren brave stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. As the son of Chief Hawkwind, he helps guide novice tauren taking their very first steps into the world. He directs young hunters and warriors through their earliest trials to test their resolve and honor their ancestors. Standing proudly beside the braves and elders of Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind bears both the proud lineage of Chief Hawkwind and the responsibility of preparing the tribe's youth. He serves as an initial mentor for new arrivals on the Red Cloud Mesa, assessing their readiness to serve the Shu'halo. By assigning trials that test stamina, tracking, and survival against local beasts such as plainstriders and mountain cougars, Grull ensures that young tauren understand that balance and respect for nature are foundational to life in Mulgore.

npc:grunt-dogran.text: Grunt Dogran. Grunt Dogran is an orc soldier of the Horde held prisoner deep within the quilboar territory of the southern Barrens. Originally assigned to the Crossroads and later Camp Taurajo, his patrol met with disaster during a raid on Agama'gor. Following his promotion within the Horde military, Grunt Dogran was dispatched from the Crossroads to reinforce Camp Taurajo. While leading a detachment of grunts into the bristled territory of Agama'gor, his unit clashed fiercely with the Bristleback quilboar. Severely injured and crippled during the fray, Dogran could not be carried away by his retreating comrades and was dragged into captivity.

npc:grunt-logmar.text: Grunt Logmar. Grunt Logmar is an orc warrior of the Horde stationed in the southern Barrens at Camp Taurajo. Dutiful and vigilant, he monitors threats surrounding the camp and coordinates efforts to locate and aid missing Horde scouts in the region. Stationed among the tauren at Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar serves as a watchful orc guard on the southern Barrens frontier. The settlement sits close to hostile quilboar grounds and the mountain passes leading into Stonetalon and Mulgore, requiring constant vigilance. Logmar coordinates scouting reports and reaches out to capable Horde travelers when his comrades find themselves ambushed or captured by local hostiles.

npc:grunth.text: Grunth. Grunth is an energetic young orc orphan living under the care of the Orgrimmar orphanage in the Drag. During Children's Week, he eagerly accompanies Horde champions on grand journeys across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what it means to be a hero. Residing in the Drag of Orgrimmar under the watchful gaze of Orphan Matron Battlewail, Grunth represents the next generation of the newly established Horde. Like many young greenskins raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he looks upon armored adventurers with wide-eyed awe and an inexhaustible stream of questions—wondering whether armored warriors are truly terrifying, why lightning on water doesn't kill every fish, and whether he will ever see someone fight an actual dragon. When festival season arrives, adventurers blow an Orcish Orphan Whistle to summon Grunth and take him on an expansive tour across the world. His bucket list spans the breadth of the Horde's domain: seeking an audience with High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof in Mulgore, venturing into the ruined throne room of Lordaeron, and visiting the rugged frontiers where his people fight for their future.

npc:guard-berton.text: Guard Berton. Guard Berton is a human town guardsman stationed outside the Lakeshire Inn in Redridge Mountains. Frustrated by the bureaucratic delays of Stormwind's legal system, he seeks swift justice against Targorr the Dread, an imprisoned orc leader. While Redridge Mountains buckles under the threat of the Blackrock orc invasion, Guard Berton remains posted outside the Lakeshire Inn. Despite local defenses being pushed to the brink, Berton's attention is fixed on a captive enemy: Targorr the Dread. Targorr was captured and locked away deep within the Stormwind Stockade, sentenced to death for his crimes against the kingdom. Yet with Stormwind's execution postponed indefinitely, Berton refuses to let the brutal raider linger in a cell while Lakeshire bleeds. Taking matters into his own hands, he hires willing adventurers to bypass royal delays and execute the orc directly.

npc:guard-howe.text: Guard Howe. Guard Howe is a town guardsman stationed near the southern foot of the Lakeshire bridge in the Redridge Mountains. Driven by a personal vendetta against the Blackrock orcs encroaching on the valley, he offers bounties to any adventurer willing to cut down the invaders. Positioned just south of the large stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill, Guard Howe stands watch over the heart of Lakeshire. Like many in the beleaguered town, he sees the encroaching Blackrock orcs as an existential threat to Redridge. Harbouring a bitter desire for revenge against the clan, Howe actively recruits passing mercenaries to hunt orcs in the eastern hills, offering pay in exchange for tangible proof of their defeat.

npc:gubber-blump.text: Gubber Blump. Gubber Blump is a dwarf fisherman and trainer stationed along the shores of Auberdine in Darkshore. Positioned on the sands between the docks and the flight master, he is an enthusiastic lover of the angling craft and seafood, particularly fresh crab meat. While most dwarves find comfort beneath stone or beside a roaring forge, Gubber Blump prefers the misty coastline of Darkshore. Stationed along the beach at Auberdine, between the flight master and the ferry pier, Gubber teaches the art of fishing and sells basic angling gear to passing travelers. He holds a deep culinary appreciation for crab meat, though he frequently relies on adventurers to help secure his catches along the dangerous coast, as well as reclaim sentimental family fishing tackle. Gubber is known to share candid stories about his family, notably his cousin Graun Blump, whom he insists possesses both a beard and an unusual odor. Travelers who lend a hand with his coastal errands—whether hauling in crawler legs or retrieving his family pole—often earn a thoughtful handwritten letter of thanks from Gubber, usually accompanied by a shiny fishing lure to encourage their future casts.

npc:gurda-ragescar.text: Gurda Ragescar. Gurda Ragescar was an orc stationed at a small Horde outpost southwest of Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Alongside Feran Strongwind, she fell defending their camp against local perils in the shadowed forest. Resting just southwest of the fortified walls of Splintertree Post, Gurda Ragescar maintained a modest Horde camp under the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Deep within territory contested by night elven defenders and wild beasts, maintaining such isolated positions is perilous work. Gurda, along with Feran Strongwind and their detachment of guards, was ultimately overrun and killed at their post, leaving only the remnants of their final stand for passing allies to discover. Travelers wandering near the trail may come across the tragic scene of Gurda's defeat. Even in death, the possessions and tasks carried by her encampment offer clues to Horde endeavors across the woods, including missing documents and orders disrupted by the ambush.

npc:hagar-lightninghoof.text: Hagar Lightninghoof. Hagar Lightninghoof is a tauren scout stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Driven by rumors of a strange clutch hidden in the canyon depths, he investigates reports of an alien egg guarded fiercely by local wind serpents. While stationed among the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof caught wind of rumors regarding an unnatural egg nestled deep inside a cavern below. The local wind serpents guarded the nest with unusual ferocity, keeping curious scouts at bay. Seeking an adventurer bold enough to brave the serpents' den, Hagar hopes to study the specimen firsthand and discern what manner of beast could warrant such defensive instincts from the canyon's natural predators.

npc:halaan-hawk-eye.text: Halaan Hawk-Eye. Halaan Hawk-Eye is a Skyborne lookout stationed atop the watchtower of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Lacking both magical sensitivity and the mystic skysight of his peers, he relies instead on keen mundane vision to monitor the surrounding island. From his perch, he tracks the distant anchor pylons and warns visitors of their faltering arcane stability. Perched high above Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye serves his people without the gifts common to many Skyborne. He cannot draw upon the arcane power flowing through the ley lines beneath Zephras Isle, nor can he gaze between worlds through the mystical skysight. Instead, Halaan relies entirely on his sharp natural senses. From his vantage point on the watchtower, he scans the horizon to observe the island's anchor pylons, calling attention to their increasingly volatile and inconsistent arcane energies.

npc:hana-zua.text: Hana'zua. Hana'zua is a Darkspear troll scout stationed in the Valley of Trials who fell victim to the poisonous beasts prowling the canyon ridges. Stricken and wounded by the monstrous scorpid Sarkoth, he lies awaiting assistance from young Horde initiates seeking to prove their valor. While traversing the arid heights overlooking the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua encountered Sarkoth, an exceptionally vicious and venomous scorpid that stalks the cliffs. Overwhelmed and stung by the beast, the troll barely survived the confrontation. Unable to move or return to camp on his own, he languishes amid the dust, counting on passing recruits to finish the creature and deliver word of his plight back to the Den.

npc:hands-springsprocket.text: Hands Springsprocket. Hands Springsprocket is an industrious gnome stationed at the entrance of Coldridge Pass in Dun Morogh. He coordinates shipments between the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley and the town of Kharanos, though recent trogg incursions have severely hampered his efforts. Perched at the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket finds his regular supply runs thoroughly disrupted. He routinely delivers provisions to the Thunderbrew distillery and the inn in Kharanos, but hostile Rockjaw troggs have overrun the subterranean tunnel leading out of the valley. With trade and foot traffic halted by the beasts, Hands is forced to rely on capable travelers to carry essential crates through the dangerous mountain corridor.

npc:hansel-heavyhands.text: Hansel Heavyhands. Hansel Heavyhands is an unusually massive Dark Iron dwarf stationed with the Thorium Brotherhood atop Thorium Point in the Searing Gorge. Tasked with perilous field work by the outpost's overseers, he consistently delegates dangerous jobs to passing adventurers using a colorful array of petty physical complaints. His hulking frame stands out among his kin, even if his enthusiasm for fieldwork does not match his size. Even by the broad-shouldered standards of the Dark Iron clan, Hansel Heavyhands is an anomaly. Towering over his brethren with a massive frame that borders on orcish in width and height, his sheer physical presence suggests a warrior built for frontline slaughter. Yet despite his imposing build and formidable moniker, Hansel appears utterly uninterested in unnecessary physical exertion, preferring the relative security of the Thorium Brotherhood's camp high above the volcanic ash. Taskmaster Scrange and Master Smith Burninate frequently assign Hansel the grim chore of culling the fiery beasts lurking in the slag pits below. When told to clear out the predatory Incendosaurs crawling through the Cauldron, Hansel begs off citing sore feet. When ordered to exterminate the Greater Lava Spiders infesting the searing wastes, he claims the blasted volcanic ridge is afflicted with a 'frigid climate' that has given him a miserable cold. Consequently, any mercenary willing to brave the magma flows finds Hansel ready with an open contract.

npc:harb-clawhoof.text: Harb Clawhoof. Harb Clawhoof is a tauren mount breeder stationed just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He tends to the tribe's sturdy kodos, offering them to worthy tauren riders and trusted champions of Thunder Bluff. Situated near the pens of Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof spends his days tending the massive kodo beasts that serve as the backbone of tauren travel and labor. Built to carry immense weight across vast distances, these sturdy animals are essential to life on the plains. Harb ensures each beast is well-cared for, disciplined, and matched only with riders who command the respect of the tauren people. While tauren naturally earn the trust required to ride Harb's kodos, outsiders face stricter scrutiny. Due to their immense size and temperament, kodos are not easily guided by those unfamiliar with their nature. Non-tauren allies who wish to ride away atop one of Harb's prized mounts must first prove their loyalty and earn exalted status with Thunder Bluff.

npc:harken-windtotem.text: Harken Windtotem. Harken Windtotem is a tauren huntsman residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Dedicated to the traditions of his people, he tasks young hunters and travelers with proving their tracking and foraging skills across the golden plains. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem serves as an instructor and guide for those learning the hunting ways of the tauren. Life on the plains of Mulgore demands respect for the natural world alongside the practical skill to sustain one's tribe. Harken evaluates young adventurers by directing them to hunt the native swoops that circle the mesas, collecting their quills to gauge a hunter's patience, aim, and ability to harvest without waste.

npc:harlan-bagley.text: Harlan Bagley. Harlan Bagley is a human armorer and merchant operating out of the Lionheart Armory in Stormwind City's bustling Trade District. He tends his shop on the northern side of the district center, looking after arms and equipment for citizens and visiting adventurers alike. Situated along the northern side of the Trade District, the Lionheart Armory serves as a steady commercial fixture within the heart of Stormwind. From behind his counter, Harlan Bagley manages inventory and deals in defensive gear, relying on incoming trade and regional couriers to keep his shelves stocked while the capital contends with distant border conflicts and supply constraints.

npc:harlo-barnaby.text: Harlo Barnaby. Harlo Barnaby is a wounded dwarven refugee residing in Menethil Harbor. Having barely escaped the slaughter when the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr, he now alerts travelers to the tragedy that unfolded in the northern marshes. Harlo Barnaby lived in Dun Modr until the northern stronghold fell to a sudden, savage assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. In the chaos of the ambush, Harlo fled south toward safety, only to catch a stray axe square in the back. Knocked unconscious by the blow, he somehow survived the trek across the marshland and awoke bandaged in Menethil Harbor. Though alive, his wounds and memories of the massacre leave him unable to return, prompting him to urge Alliance adventurers to investigate the smoking ruins of his former home.

npc:hegnar-rumbleshot.text: Hegnar Rumbleshot. Hegnar Rumbleshot is a dwarven gunsmith stationed along the snowy roadway leading from Coldridge Pass toward Kharanos. He maintains a busy shooting range and equips local hunters and mountaineers with firearms and ammunition. Set up at a small campsite between Coldridge Pass and Kharanos, Hegnar Rumbleshot caters to dwarven marksmen, travelers, and the local militia. His camp features a popular shooting range where mountain folk hone their aim against the wild beasts prowling Dun Morogh. Supplying so many eager shooters means Hegnar burns through munitions at a brisk pace, leaving him perpetually reliant on fresh shipments of ammunition from his supplier, the dwarf engineer Loslor Rudge.

npc:henze-faulk.text: Henze Faulk. Henze Faulk is a dwarven adventurer found lying near death on the stone circle outside Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest. Struck down by the Defias Brotherhood while shielding his companion, he serves as a pivotal test for aspiring paladins learning to wield the gift of resurrection. Near the ancient stone ring east of Stormwind sits Heroes' Vigil, a place often haunted by Defias bandits prowling the Elwynn woods. Henze Faulk and his friend Gazin Tenorm were ambushed here by Defias marauders. Putting himself in harm's way to ensure Gazin's survival, Henze fell to the bandits' blades. While his companion survived to summon aid from the Cathedral of Light, Henze's body remains on the threshold of life and death, awaiting the divine intervention of a paladin carrying a Symbol of Life.

npc:heralath-fallowbrook.text: Heralath Fallowbrook. Heralath Fallowbrook is a dying night elf druid imprisoned deep within Razorfen Kraul. Dispatched to investigate the thorny corruption surrounding the remains of the Ancient Agamaggan, he was captured and brutalized by the Razorfen tribe. With his final breaths, he seeks to send word of his fate and a cherished pendant back to his wife in Darnassus. Sent by his people to investigate the ancient boar god Agamaggan and the spreading briars choking the southern Barrens, Heralath Fallowbrook sought the root of Razorfen Kraul's corruption. Instead of unearthing answers, the night elf was taken prisoner by the quilboar. Locked in a squalid pen and relentlessly beaten, Heralath succumbed to severe wounds and raging fever. Before fading entirely, he shared what he knew with a fellow captive, the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow, urging him to warn the sentinel outpost at Thalanaar about the aggression stirred up by the quilboar crone Charlga Razorflank.

npc:high-executor-derrington.text: High Executor Derrington. High Executor Derrington commands the Forsaken vanguard stationed at the Bulwark on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades. A no-nonsense military officer, he oversees the Horde's front-line defense against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade threats emanating from the Western Plaguelands. From this fortified barricade, he directs seasoned champions toward contested ruins like Andorhal and Scholomance. Standing directly before the fortified barricades of the Bulwark, High Executor Derrington serves as the gatekeeper between the haunted safety of Tirisfal Glades and the rotting horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Derrington holds little patience for political maneuvering in the Undercity, viewing the front lines as a crucible of sheer survival. For Horde soldiers and sellswords seeking to test their mettle, Derrington provides direct military orders, sending scouts and strike teams deep into plagueridden territory to blunt enemy incursions before they breach Tirisfal. Derrington's defensive position is beleaguered on multiple axes. To the east lies the Scourge, entrenched in the shattered town of Andorhal and spilling through the countryside via corrupting cauldrons. Simultaneously, the zealous fanatics of the Scarlet Crusade contest northern fortifications and skirmish relentlessly with Forsaken patrols. Derrington coordinates surgical counterattacks, sabotage against the Scarlet lines, and the systematic disruption of Scourge cauldron fields to safeguard the eastern border.

npc:high-priest-rohan.text: High Priest Rohan. High Priest Rohan is the preeminent leader of the Church of the Holy Light within Ironforge, found pacing inside the Hall of Mysteries. He oversees the spiritual development of fledgling priests across the Alliance and aids those seeking mastery over the Holy Light. Through his guidance and sacred relics, he maintains spiritual ties between the mountain kingdom, Stormwind, and distant allies. Pacing the quiet flagstones of the Hall of Mysteries in the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan acts as the highest-ranking representative of the Church of the Holy Light in Ironforge. While dwarves historically honored the titans, dwarven priests have deeply embraced the Light's virtues of wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan serves as a patient teacher to young acolytes, teaching them the discipline necessary to channel holy magic and steel their minds against despair. Rohan recognizes that spiritual insight takes many shapes across the Alliance. Once priests under his tutelage grasp the fundamentals, he directs them outward—sending human and dwarven students to High Priestess Laurena in Stormwind City, or dispatching night elf disciples to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to master elusive mysteries like Elune's Grace. Beyond the capitals, he urges devotees to render assistance wherever hardship strikes, even directing healers abroad to aid the druids of the Cenarion Circle in distant Azshara. In addition to his teachings, Rohan holds custody over sacred relics essential to the wider Alliance priesthood and paladin brotherhoods. Among his possessions is a blessed exorcism censer, seasoned through years of cleansing vile spirits. When the Order of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker require the vessel to temper the holy calling of their knights, Rohan freely yields it—asking only for charitable alms to replenish Ironforge's dwindling food reserves for the city's needy.

npc:highlord-demitrian.text: Highlord Demitrian. Highlord Demitrian is a solitary human hermit dwelling amidst the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus. Describing himself as a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan, he possesses the esoteric knowledge required to wake the slumbering elemental lord. Adventurers bearing ancient elemental bindings seek him out to unlock the power of the Windseeker. Found lingering at an abandoned encampment in the Crystal Vale, Demitrian appears out of place in the desolate wastes of Silithus. Though he is tied to the Twilight's Hammer whose ravaged camp he haunts, Demitrian acts above all as a herald for Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He treats visitors with aloof indifference unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

npc:hogger.text: Hogger. Hogger is the vicious chieftain of the Riverpaw gnolls prowling southwestern Elwynn Forest. Towering over his kin and remarkably aggressive, he has become notorious for raiding local farms and butchering unsuspecting travelers. His violent rampages have earned him an official bounty from the Stormwind Marshals. Prowling atop Hogger Hill in southwestern Elwynn Forest, Hogger commands the local Riverpaw pack with unmatched savagery. In the years following the Third War, gnoll raids across local homesteads grew increasingly bold and coordinated. Behind this rise in violence lies an unsettling alliance: the Riverpaw have begun colluding with the Defias Brotherhood, trading raw ferocity for arms, tactical direction, and magical support. To safeguard Elwynn's borders and protect trade routes from further bloodshed, Marshal Dughan has posted a generous bounty on Hogger's head.

npc:holt-thunderhorn.text: Holt Thunderhorn. Holt Thunderhorn is a tauren hunter trainer stationed upon Hunter Rise in the elevated city of Thunder Bluff. He instructs novice and seasoned track-masters in their craft, offering basic martial guidance and pointing maturing marksmen toward specialized trials across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on Hunter Rise above the sweeping plains of Mulgore, Holt Thunderhorn serves the Horde as a seasoned instructor in ranged combat, tracking, and survival. Like many elders of his craft, he guides young tauren as they make the transition from roaming hunters into disciplined defenders of their new capital.

npc:huldar.text: Huldar. Huldar is a dwarven teamster stationed along the southern road of Loch Modan, near the shores of the lake. Tasked with hauling vital blast powder to the dig site in the south, his delivery caravan faces relentless harassment from local threats and Dark Iron saboteurs. Hauling explosives through Loch Modan is no simple trade route. Huldar was tasked with driving wagonloads of mining blast powder down toward the southern excavation site, where dwarven archaeologists and prospectors desperately need supplies. However, the wilderness roads have become increasingly hazardous. With local wildlife, troggs, and Dark Iron infiltrators lurking near the lake's southern bend, Huldar finds himself stranded by his damaged wagon, relying on wandering travelers to safeguard the remaining powder kegs and ensure the shipment reaches the dig.

npc:illiyana-moonblaze.text: Illiyana Moonblaze. Illiyana Moonblaze is a night elf supply officer stationed at Silverwing Grove in Ashenvale. Operating alongside the Silverwing Sentinels, she supplies Alliance champions waging war against the Warsong Outriders. Illiyana Moonblaze serves as the supply officer for the Silverwing Sentinels nestled in Silverwing Grove. From her post near the path into Warsong Gulch, she outfits the defenders who hold the southern woods of Ashenvale against the Warsong clan. Beyond keeping the grove's stores, Illiyana equips Alliance volunteers preparing to clash with the Warsong clan in Warsong Gulch. As champions earn favor with the Silverwing Sentinels, she rewards their service with custom rations, specialized draughts, and masterwork armaments designed specifically for woodland skirmishes. She also maintains weapons and armor for weary fighters returning from the frontline, keeping the Sentinels' war effort supplied and functional.

npc:ilthalaine.text: Ilthalaine. Ilthalaine is a night elf guardian standing watch over the sacred glade of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. He serves as the primary greeter and mentor for young night elves taking their very first steps into the world. Vigilant and attuned to the wilderness, he guides novice adventurers toward maintaining the delicate balance of nature across the boughs of the World Tree. Positioned just outside the heart of Shadowglen, Ilthalaine is often the first face a fledgling night elf sees upon beginning their journey. He observes the woodland paths and notices the subtle shifts within the forest that go unseen by ordinary eyes. His duty is to welcome returning kin and ensure that any newly awakened defenders are grounded in the traditions of their people, ready to face the responsibilities that come with tending to Teldrassil. Heavy spring rains have allowed the nightsaber and thistle boar populations in Shadowglen to grow beyond what the glade can feed. Ilthalaine asks young defenders to thin their numbers so that the woodland's other creatures can flourish and nature's balance can be preserved. Beyond testing an adventurer's martial prowess against local wildlife, Ilthalaine directs young elves toward their chosen callings. Entrusting each traveler with a class sigil, he points them directly to their mentors within the Aldrassil sanctuary—whether they follow the path of the warrior, druid, rogue, priest, or hunter. Through him, every novice learns where their service to the Kaldorei begins.

npc:innkeeper-allison.text: Innkeeper Allison. Innkeeper Allison manages the Gilded Rose, one of the busiest and most central inns in Stormwind City. Located in the heart of the Trade District right between the bank and auction house, she provides weary travelers and local merchants with hearthstone bindings, refreshing drinks, and shelter. Positioned squarely between the bustling trade auction house and the main city vaults, the Gilded Rose serves as an epicenter for adventurers arriving in Stormwind. Innkeeper Allison stands behind the main counter on the ground floor, keeping order amidst a constant flow of peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. Beyond offering lodging and hearthstone services, she frequently participates in local holiday festivities and coordinates small errands for traveling heroes seeking rest within the capital.

npc:innkeeper-farley.text: Innkeeper Farley. Innkeeper Farley manages the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, providing food, lodging, and hearthstones to travelers passing through Elwynn Forest. Well-liked and observant, he often holds misplaced mail and listens to the troubles of adventurers on the road. Innkeeper Farley runs the Lion's Pride Inn with a welcoming hand and a sharp eye. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall and Duskwood stop at his counter for a warm meal, a mug of ale and a bed, and Farley keeps order in one of the realm's busiest waystations, pouring ale and serving cheese to all who pass through Goldshire.

npc:innkeeper-firebrew.text: Innkeeper Firebrew. Innkeeper Firebrew manages the Stonefire Tavern in the bustling Commons of Ironforge. A genial host to weary mountaineers and visiting dignitaries alike, he serves hearty dwarven staples and keeps travelers rested beneath the mountain. Situated in the central ring of the Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew's establishment is often the first sanctuary encountered by travelers entering through the Great Gates of Ironforge. Behind a counter laden with flagons of ale, skins of stout, and roasted joints of meat, Firebrew offers hospitality to adventurers bound for the snowy passes of Dun Morogh or deeper into the mountain kingdom. His tavern remains a lively crossroad where miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather to escape the drafty tunnels and exchange tales around the hearth.

npc:innkeeper-grosk.text: Innkeeper Grosk. Innkeeper Grosk manages the inn at Razor Hill, providing weary travelers with food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Located on the bustling road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar, his establishment serves as the primary resting point for young Horde adventurers setting out into the wider world. Razor Hill serves as the vital crossroad settlement connecting the southern training grounds of Durotar to the high walls of Orgrimmar. At the center of this waystation stands Innkeeper Grosk, an orc tasked with sheltering warriors, scouts, and peons alike. His inn offers a respite from the harsh desert heat, stocked with basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water for any traveler passing beneath its sturdy timbers. Beyond serving passing travelers, Grosk assists the local labor force that keeps Durotar running. In the quest 'A Peon's Burden', the timid peon Ukor, who hauled food all the way to the Valley of Trials only to find it was not needed, asks travelers to carry the load back to Grosk's inn in Razor Hill.

npc:innkeeper-gryshka.text: Innkeeper Gryshka. Innkeeper Gryshka is an orc host who manages the Broken Tusk inn in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Serving as the primary hospitality contact for travelers arriving through the city gates, she provides hearthstone bindings, food, and drink to visiting Horde adventurers. She maintains close ties with hunters and scouts across Durotar and the Barrens to keep her tavern stocked with choice cuts of meat. Standing behind the counter of the Broken Tusk, Gryshka manages one of the most heavily trafficked inns in the Horde. Located just beyond the main gates of Orgrimmar in the Valley of Strength, her establishment serves as the first point of rest for warriors, messengers, and newly arrived champions seeking shelter under Thrall's banner. Running a bustling tavern in an arid canyon requires steady supply lines. Gryshka maintains a well-known affinity for fresh meat, relying on trusted hunters across the Horde territories to supply her kitchen. Companions such as Zargh in the Crossroads and Grimtak in Durotar routinely ship their finest game cuts back to the Broken Tusk to satisfy her demanding culinary standards.

npc:innkeeper-keldamyr.text: Innkeeper Keldamyr. Innkeeper Keldamyr manages the hearth and lodgings of the central inn in Dolanaar, Teldrassil. He offers food, drink, and a resting place for young night elves venturing forth from Shadowglen into the wider boughs of the World Tree. Dolanaar is the primary village newcomers reach after departing the sheltered glade of Aldrassil. Innkeeper Keldamyr maintains the community's central haven, providing bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath the canopy of Teldrassil. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus frequently pause at his counter to rest their spirits, secure their hearthstones, and stock rations for the journey through the boughs. Running an inn high within the branches requires steady supply lines from nearby settlements and tradesfolk. Local couriers often find themselves directed straight to Keldamyr's desk to drop off goods, linking him directly into the daily trade and logistics keeping the settlement of Dolanaar running smoothly.

npc:innkeeper-norman.text: Innkeeper Norman. Innkeeper Norman tends the hearth at the primary tavern in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity. A quiet, diligent Forsaken, he offers travelers of the Horde respite, hearthstone bindings, and food suited to the varied tastes of both the living and the dead. Located in the bustling Trade Quarter beneath the ruined Capital City of Lordaeron, Innkeeper Norman provides lodging for emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold. Despite the damp chill and alchemical stenches of the Undercity, Norman's tavern remains a bustling hub for travelers looking to anchor their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for expeditions into the Plaguelands. While Norman typically keeps to his duties selling provisions and managing rooms, the seasonal arrival of Hallow's End reveals a more peculiar side. During the holiday, Norman participates in the seasonal revelry, demanding peculiar displays—such as clucking like a chicken—from adventurous patrons eager to earn holiday treats like Undercity mints.

npc:innkeeper-pala.text: Innkeeper Pala. Innkeeper Pala manages the Cat and the Shaman, the bustling tavern situated on the lower tier of Thunder Bluff. She offers visiting adventurers a hearthstone binding, cold drinks, and a place to rest between journeys across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on the lower rise of Thunder Bluff's sweeping mesas, Innkeeper Pala tends the hearth at the Cat and the Shaman. The establishment serves as one of the primary gathering points for travelers stepping off the central lifts or arriving from the sprawling plains of Mulgore. Holding a steady vigil over her common room, Pala ensures that weary warriors, wandering druids, and visiting allies of the Horde find a dependable shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar home away from home.

npc:jahan-hawkwing.text: Jahan Hawkwing. Jahan Hawkwing is a tauren armorer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. He provides essential leather and chainmail gear to travelers braving the harsh, predator-filled plains. Situated at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Jahan Hawkwing tends to the equipment needs of Horde wanderers and defenders. The Barrens is a brutal expanse where durable protective gear often makes the difference between survival and falling to centaur, quilboar, or wild beasts. Jahan works alongside local leatherworkers, handling deliveries of cured hides to keep his shop stocked with reliable tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

npc:james-halloran.text: James Halloran. James Halloran is a human tanner working out of the Wetlands to supply fine hides across the eastern continents. Based in Menethil Harbor, he makes a living harvesting the tough, prized skins of the region's native crocolisks. He relies on passing travelers and nearby trade channels to gather raw materials and transport his finished leathers to market. From his home in Menethil Harbor, James Halloran makes his living from the marshland just outside town. As an enterprising tanner, Halloran recognized that the perilous bogs offer a lucrative commodity: crocolisk skins. Transforming the rugged hide of marsh reptiles into high-quality leather requires rare craftsmanship, and Halloran's finished goods are shipped out through local trade channels to buyers all across Azeroth. Operating so close to the marsh comes with constant danger. Halloran cannot easily hunt every beast himself while tending to curing vats and trade logistics. He frequently hires hardy travelers to handle the rougher chores of skinning young marsh beasts and managing routine deliveries between his work site and surrounding settlements, ensuring his bustling leather craft stays fully supplied.

npc:jannok-breezesong.text: Jannok Breezesong. Jannok Breezesong is a night elf rogue trainer stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He offers instruction in stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to young kaldorei rogues venturing out into the boughs of the World Tree. Found lounging beneath the boughs of Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong serves as the primary instructor for novice night elf rogues. Unlike the formal sentinels or cloistered druids of Teldrassil, Jannok guides those who operate quietly on the fringes of society, teaching them how to stalk the shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen amidst the boughs. Once a rogue has advanced beyond initial lessons in Dolanaar, Jannok directs them onward to more experienced masters in the capital city of Darnassus.

npc:jasper-fel.text: Jasper Fel. Jasper Fel is a discreet supplier operating out of the SI:7 headquarters in Stormwind's Old Town. Providing daggers and assorted vials to operatives, he keeps a sharp eye on visitors and warns them to watch their tongues. His quiet trade supports the covert arm of the kingdom behind closed doors. Tucked away inside the barracks of SI:7 within Old Town, Jasper Fel caters to a very specific clientele. Rather than hawking standard arms to the city guard, he provides essential implements of tradecraft: simple daggers and the delicate vials required for brewing and applying poisons. Fel operates under the strict discipline of Mathias Shaw's intelligence division, curtly advising any who approach to mind their speech. In a stronghold dedicated to espionage and subtle lethality, casual chatter is an easy way to meet an early end.

npc:jen-shan.text: Jen'shan. Jen'shan is a Darkspear jungle troll and hunter trainer stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. She guides fledgling orc and troll marksmen as they take their first steps into the wilds of the Horde. Young hunters are directed to her to learn the basics of tracking, ranged combat, and survival. Perched among the weathered encampments of the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan serves as the primary hunter mentor for new recruits proving their worth to the Horde. Together, young orcs and Darkspear trolls arrive clutching inscribed tablets and parchments directing them straight to her side. With keen eyes sharpened by years in the untamed wilderness, she imparts foundational techniques in archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, ensuring no novice falls prey to the scorpids and boars prowling the canyon floor.

npc:jennea-cannon.text: Jennea Cannon. Jennea Cannon is a respected human mage trainer residing within the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. She oversees the education of novice sorcerers, guiding them through foundational studies and investigating disturbances in the flow of local arcane energies. Through her tasks, she tests whether apprentices have the discipline needed to control magic without being consumed by it. Positioned atop the spiral walkway of the Wizard's Sanctum, Jennea Cannon stands as one of the primary mentors for arcane practitioners entering Stormwind. Rather than merely drilling spells into pupils, she emphasizes caution and self-control. To non-mages passing through the tower, she offers a sharp warning: unchecked magic will burn the untrained, a truth novice spellcasters learn quickly under her tutelage. Jennea believes magical theory must be tested by real-world observation. She frequently dispatches promising apprentices outside the city walls, sending them to examine sites such as Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest to understand how natural water sources interact with arcane resonance. As students advance, she tests their resolve by directing them to investigate disruptions at the Blue Recluse or gathering volatile reagents for crafting their first true wizard's implements. While Jennea handles early instruction and local affairs, she knows when an apprentice has outgrown her syllabus. Once an initiate demonstrates true potential, she directs them up the hierarchy of the Sanctum to High Sorcerer Andromath or even beyond the kingdom's borders to reclusive practitioners like Tabetha deep in the Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:jocaste.text: Jocaste. Jocaste is a night elf hunter trainer residing within the verdant Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Working alongside the Cenarion Circle, she mentors young night elf marksmen and beastmasters who arrive from the wilds of Teldrassil. Stationed among the tranquil groves of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Jocaste serves as an instructor for night elf hunters. When fledgling trackers finish their initial training in Shadowglen and venture into the capital city, Jocaste guides their transition into seasoned survivalists. She teaches the arts of marksmanship, wilderness survival, and the sacred bond between a hunter and the wild beasts of Kalimdor.

npc:john-j-keeshan.text: John J. Keeshan. Corporal John J. Keeshan is a human soldier of Stormwind's army who fought the Blackrock orcs in the Redridge Mountains. After being captured during the fighting around Stonewatch, he was dragged deep into Render's Rock as a prisoner of war. John J. Keeshan is a corporal in the service of Stormwind, posted to the Redridge Mountains as the Blackrock orcs pressed against Lakeshire and its defenders. When the fighting flared up around Stonewatch Keep, Keeshan was in the thick of it alongside the other soldiers holding the line for the kingdom.

npc:jorah-annison.text: Jorah Annison. Jorah Annison is a Forsaken cartographer stationed in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Though his profession revolves around maps and geography, his expertise proves invaluable to traveling spellcasters in search of obscure, scattered knowledge across Azeroth. Dwelling amidst the alchemical vapors and arcane echoes of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Jorah Annison plies the trade of cartography. Yet the maps bore him: Jorah would trade every one in the shop for a single good book, and he knows more of ancient texts than almost anyone, a scholar's taste he shares with the warlocks who seek him out. Jorah's knowledge of the land extends well beyond the ruins of Lordaeron. Warlocks seeking the elusive Tome of the Cabal are frequently directed to him to uncover where ancient texts and remnants of dark sects might be salvaged, bridging the gap between historical lore and distant geography.

npc:jorgen.text: Jorgen. Jorgen is a discreet human informant residing in Stormwind City, tucked away by the water just inside the Valley of Heroes. Despite his modest and out-of-the-way perch, he is entangled in sensitive matters involving prominent figures in the capital, including Elling Trias and Bishop DeLavey. Positioned down near the water immediately to the right of Stormwind's monumental entryway, Jorgen maintains a low profile away from the bustling thoroughfares of the city. While the towering statues of heroes overlook the bridge above, Jorgen monitors comings and goings from the shadows below, serving as a quiet contact for those who need information kept off the record.

npc:josef-gregorian.text: Josef Gregorian. Josef Gregorian is a Forsaken tailoring trainer found working in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. He guides ambitious Horde tailors seeking to weave enchanted fabrics, providing expertise and directing them toward specialized garments. Amid the dim alchemical lanterns and damp vaults of the Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian maintains the fine craft of tailoring for the Forsaken and their Horde allies. While life in the subterranean kingdom has turned cold, cloth-working remains vital for warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian serves as a dependable instructor in the capital, ready to teach foundational patterns and to stitch the first robes of young mages who bring him the right materials.

npc:kaal-soulreaper.text: Kaal Soulreaper. Kaal Soulreaper is an orc warlock trainer stationed deep within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Despite dwelling among the Forsaken, he maintains close ties to fellow practitioners of the dark arts across the Horde, frequently guiding apprentices to mentors in distant lands. While Thrall's Horde strictly regulates and monitors fel magic within Orgrimmar, practitioners like Kaal Soulreaper find ample harbor in the subterranean sanctums of Lordaeron. Residing within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Kaal shares his mastery over demonic entities and curses with Horde warlocks willing to learn. Beyond basic instruction, he acts as an essential contact for practitioners seeking greater power, directing ambitious students across the sea to mentors like Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

npc:kali-remik.text: Kali Remik. Kali Remik is a Darkspear troll hunter who spends her time lending guidance to travelers across the Horde's heartland. Familiar with the ways of tracking and survival in Durotar, she directs young hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill to learn the taming of beasts. Kali Remik is a seasoned jungle troll tracker well-acquainted with the arid wastes of Durotar and the bustling hubs of the Horde. In coastal settlements like Sen'jin Village, she watches over young scouts taking their first steps outside the Valley of Trials. Knowing when a novice outgrows the local training grounds, she steps in to direct promising marksmen toward Thotar in Razor Hill to begin their path as beastmasters, ensuring the Horde's frontier ranks stay sharp and disciplined.

npc:kaltunk.text: Kaltunk. Kaltunk is an orc overseer stationed at the heart of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He serves as the very first point of contact for young orcs taking their opening steps into the world. It is his duty to welcome these aspiring champions and direct them to their initial duties in service to the Horde. Standing under the harsh sun of the Valley of Trials, Kaltunk watches over the newly arrived hopefuls seeking to prove themselves worthy of the Horde. While other trainers and elders assign grueling trials and hunting rites, Kaltunk ensures that no recruit wanders aimlessly through the red dust. He delivers straightforward orders, pointing newcomers directly toward Gornek and the path of discipline. The Valley of Trials is not an easy proving ground; it was chosen specifically to forge strength and resilience in every youth who walks its canyon floors. Kaltunk embodies this rugged practicality. He offers no grand speeches or coddling, expecting each orc to quickly find their place in the world and pull their weight for the warchief.

npc:kanati-greycloud.text: Kanati Greycloud. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter stationed at Whitereach Post within Thousand Needles. Alongside his hunting companions, he musters what defense he can while enduring constant hostility from the local Galak centaur. Kanati Greycloud makes his camp at Whitereach Post, high atop the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. While the canyon offers abundant game and open vistas, it is hemmed in by the Galak centaur, whose warbands contest every inch of the arid flats below. Together with other tauren hunters, Kanati keeps watch over the canyon floor, striving to preserve the post against the brutal depredations of the surrounding marauders.

npc:kaplak.text: Kaplak. Kaplak is an orc rogue trainer stationed in Razor Hill in central Durotar. He instructs young orcs and trolls in the arts of stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft, preparing them for service to the Horde before dispatching them into Orgrimmar. Tucked away in the settlement of Razor Hill, Kaplak serves as a foundational instructor for fledgling Horde rogues emerging from the Valley of Trials. Where traditional orc culture glorifies open combat and roaring charges, Kaplak teaches the colder, quieter disciplines necessary for survival: stalking unseen, picking locks, and striking lethal blows from behind. Once his students outgrow his tutelage in the dusty red ravines of Durotar, he directs them north to the capital of Orgrimmar to deepen their craft among senior guild operatives.

npc:karang-amakkar.text: Karang Amakkar. Karang Amakkar is an orc scout stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the rocky coast of Ashenvale. Operating on the fringe of Horde territory, he focuses on curbing the violent furbolg tribes that threaten the outpost's supply lines and borders. Adventurers travelling through the outpost rely on his local intelligence to navigate the perilous tensions of the forest. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar serves the Horde at one of its most vulnerable border outposts. The encampment faces constant pressure from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Karang keeps a close eye on the hostile native populations that surround the road eastward, ensuring that Horde couriers and scouting parties do not get ambushed by territorial indigenous tribes. Karang focuses much of his attention on the furbolg populations native to the ancient woods, notably the Foulweald tribe. With corruption and primal hostility driving these bear-folk into frenzies, Karang tasks capable warriors with culling their leader and clearing out dens before the tribes can muster organized assaults against Zoram'gar.

npc:kargal-battlescar.text: Kargal Battlescar. Kargal Battlescar is a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Far Watch Post along the eastern border of the Barrens. Tasked with guarding the crossing from Durotar, he evaluates incoming recruits and directs capable fighters deeper into the territory to bolster Horde defenses. Standing watch at the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar oversees the strategic threshold separating the harsh red plains of Durotar from the vast savanna of the Barrens. As travelers and fresh adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, Kargal ensures they understand that the peaceful days of training in the Valley of Trials are over. The Barrens is a contested and dangerous expanse, plagued by aggressive wildlife, centaur raiding parties, and quilboar tribes. Kargal inspects those who pass, mustering willing recruits into the service of the Horde and sending them onward to the Crossroads to aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

npc:karos-razok.text: Karos Razok. Karos Razok is the Forsaken bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. He oversees the roost of undead fliers that connect this contested frontier outpost directly to the Undercity and other Horde strongholds. Perched on the wooden platform above the crypts of the Sepulcher, Karos Razok tends to the skeletal bats vital for Forsaken communications. With Silverpine Forest infested by Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill, overland travel along the northern road is treacherous. Razok ensures that messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies can cross above the haunted canopy, keeping the front line linked straight back to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

npc:katie-hunter.text: Katie Hunter. Katie Hunter is a horse breeder stationed at the stables in the Eastvale Logging Camp within eastern Elwynn Forest. She provides trained riding horses and steeds to citizens of Stormwind and trusted champions of the Alliance. Alongside Randal Hunter, she ensures travelers and soldiers have reliable mounts to navigate the kingdom's roads. Tucked away in the quiet, wooded clearings of the Eastvale Logging Camp, Katie Hunter manages the kingdom's primary horse stock for aspiring riders in Elwynn Forest. While the lumberjacks harvest timber for Stormwind's reconstruction, Katie tends to the stables, raising a variety of dependable breeds including pintos, mares, and swift steeds. Her stock represents the classic equestrian tradition of the kingdom, offering faithful companions capable of braving dangerous roads across southern Azeroth.

npc:kaymard-copperpinch.text: Kaymard Copperpinch. Kaymard Copperpinch is a goblin merchant representing Smokywood Pastures in Orgrimmar during the Feast of Winter Veil. Stationed in the Valley of Strength, he hawks festive goods and directs travelers toward holiday cheer and missing holiday supplies. His brisk trade brings seasonal merriment—and Goblin commercial enterprise—to the Horde capital. When the Feast of Winter Veil arrives, Smokywood Pastures sets up shop right in the bustling Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar, fronted by the enterprising Kaymard Copperpinch. While Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby, Kaymard makes sure the season remains profitable. Selling higher-end treats, festive wrapping paper, and holiday necessities, he embodies the goblin view that no grand cultural festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin. Beyond peddling festive wares, Kaymard often serves as a point of contact for the seasonal mishaps that plague Smokywood Pastures. From stolen shipments of holiday confections to the mysterious disappearance of Metzen the Reindeer, Kaymard eagerly enlists Horde adventurers to sort out trouble in the snow and keep the festival running smoothly.

npc:keeper-albagorm.text: Keeper Albagorm. Keeper Albagorm is a keeper of the grove stationed at the idyllic sanctuary of Stonetalon Peak. Deeply concerned by the devastation corrupting the southern reaches of the mountains, he enlists travelers to help heal the scorched wilderness of the Charred Vale. Perched within the peaceful boughs of Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm stands vigil over one of Kalimdor's sacred elven refuges. Like many sons of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world acutely. His attention is drawn southward toward the smoldering ruins of the Charred Vale, set afire by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists and now held by Bloodfury harpies who block any regrowth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works tirelessly to halt the spread of the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

npc:keeper-bel-dugur.text: Keeper Bel'dugur. Keeper Bel'dugur is a scholarly Forsaken residing deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity. While ostensibly serving the interests of his people by commissioning expeditions to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts, subtle clues reveal far more sinister allegiances. Situated among the vats and researchers of the Apothecarium, Keeper Bel'dugur tasks adventurers with retrieving dangerous arcane and occult relics from across Azeroth. Among his most prominent interests is the Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on extra-dimensional beings locked away inside Shadowfang Keep. While many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure or weaponize the condition of the undead, Bel'dugur's curated acquisitions appear tailored toward unearthing ancient, forbidden powers.

npc:keeper-bel-varil.text: Keeper Bel'varil. Keeper Bel'varil is a Forsaken caretaker and researcher stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Working closely alongside Wordeen Voidglare, he directs Horde adventurers to gather magical relics and binding materials from the surrounding lands to further their occult studies. Amid the besieged village of Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil quietly supports the Forsaken's magical and alchemical research. While royal apothecaries and soldiers occupy themselves with the Alliance garrison down the road at Southshore, Bel'varil focuses on practical sorcery, dispatching travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

npc:keldran.text: Keldran. Keldran is an orc operative stationed just north of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. Dedicated to paving the way for eventual diplomacy with the Alliance, he coordinates covert strikes against demonic remnants to prove the modern Horde has truly forsaken the Burning Legion. While Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom, Keldran works from the city's red rock terraces to solve a lingering diplomatic disaster. The Alliance still views all orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation cemented during the first wars. Convinced that even Thrall tires of endless conflict, Keldran believes true peace talks can never occur while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without formal sanction from the Warchief, he takes the initiative upon himself, directing trusted agents toward distant threats to dismantle the demonic stain once and for all.

npc:kelm-hargunth.text: Kelm Hargunth. Kelm Hargunth is the primary supply officer and quartermaster for the Warsong Outriders, stationed at Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern border of the Barrens. He equips Horde champions fighting against the night elves in the contested forests of Warsong Gulch. Through his care packages and provisions, he ensures that the frontline war effort remains fully supplied. Perched on the earthen ramparts overlooking Ashenvale, Kelm Hargunth oversees logistical operations for the Warsong Outriders at Mor'shan Base Camp. While scouts and raiders skirmish beyond the stockade, Hargunth manages the flow of weapons, armor, and rations required to sustain a protracted border war. To him, victory against the Silverwing Sentinels depends as much on steady provisions as it does on raw battle fury. Hargunth distributes specialized supplies to warriors who have proven their valor in the gulch. From custom care packages stuffed with field dressings and iron rations to mastercrafted armaments bearing the crimson insignia of the Warsong clan, his stores are reserved strictly for those who bleed for the Horde's territorial ambitions in the timber-rich forests to the north.

npc:kerlonian-evershade.text: Kerlonian Evershade. Kerlonian Evershade is a night elf Druid of the Claw resting at the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore. Having recently awakened from the long slumber within the Emerald Dream, he requires aid navigating the corrupted wilds to reach the safety of Maestra's Post. Kerlonian Evershade belongs to the Druids of the Claw, followers of the bear totem who spent centuries sleeping in barrows and communion with the Emerald Dream. The Druids of the Claw were called from their slumber during the Third War. Found resting beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, Kerlonian is still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his prolonged rest. His immediate concern is traveling safely through the troubled forests of Darkshore toward Maestra's Post on the border of Ashenvale. The road out of the Grove of the Ancients is far from secure. Blackwood furbolgs prowl the Twilight Vale, and Dark Strand cultists lurk along the road into Ashenvale. Weakened from sleep and struggling with sudden bouts of exhaustion, Kerlonian relies on sympathetic travelers of the Alliance to protect him as he makes his way south to rejoin his fellow night elves.

npc:kernobee.text: Kernobee. Kernobee is a goblin engineer trapped deep within the ruined halls of Gnomeregan. After stumbling upon dangerous secrets involving Dark Iron dwarf sabotage, he was captured, beaten unconscious, and left to die among the troggs in the dormitory quarters. While conducting business or scavenging within the fallen gnome capital, Kernobee uncovered a grave secret: the Dark Iron dwarves were directly involved in the construction and operation of the massive super rig burrowing beneath the city. Realizing the immense value—and lethality—of this intelligence, he attempted to flee immediately to Ratchet to deliver word to his associate, Tinkerwiz. Unfortunately, the Dark Irons caught him before he could make his escape. Rather than killing him outright, his captors battered Kernobee unconscious and tossed him into a small room along the dormitory corridor, opposite the Clean Zone. Left stranded among feral troggs and radiation fallout, the battered goblin depends entirely on passing adventurers to revive him and shield him until he can reach safety.

npc:keryn-sylvius.text: Keryn Sylvius. Keryn Sylvius is a human rogue trainer stationed on the second floor of Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Tucked away in the inn's reading room, she teaches fledgling scoundrels the basics of stealth and bladecraft while acting as a quiet conduit to Stormwind's intelligence service. While the ground floor of the Lion's Pride Inn bustles with boisterous travelers and weary town guards, Keryn Sylvius keeps to the quiet reading room upstairs. Outwardly unassuming, she observes the constant flow of road gossip and serves as the local mentor for rogues cutting their teeth in Elwynn Forest. When promising operatives outgrow local petty thievery and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius discretely sends them onward to Stormwind City to make contact with SI:7.

npc:khelden-bremen.text: Khelden Bremen. Khelden Bremen is a human mage and instructor stationed on the upper floor of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. He oversees the earliest instruction of novice spellcasters who take up the arcane arts in service to Stormwind. Situated within the tranquil stone walls of Northshire Abbey, Khelden Bremen acts as the primary instructor for fledgling human mages. While the clergy and defenders handle martial and spiritual pursuits below, Bremen maintains a quiet study upstairs. Here, he introduces novices to the discipline, focus, and fundamental techniques required to weave raw magical energy safely before they venture out into Elwynn Forest and beyond to Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

npc:kil-hala.text: Kil'hala. Kil'hala is a jungle troll tailoring trainer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Skilled in working with both everyday cloth and exotic woven materials, he instructs Horde crafters looking to refine their needlework. Beyond common thread, he weaves nether-lace robes for young Horde mages who bring him locks of hair from the laughing sisters of Ashenvale. Positioned at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Kil'hala offers his tailoring expertise to passing travelers and Horde recruits. While much of his craft involves common spun bolts and garments fit for dry plains life, his knowledge extends into rare magical textiles. As a favor to the mage Deino, he fashions nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair taken from the laughing sisters, dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

npc:kin-weelay.text: Kin'weelay. Kin'weelay is a renowned Darkspear witch doctor stationed at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Dispatched directly from Orgrimmar, he offers mystical aid and counsel to the Horde vanguard in the jungle. His spiritual expertise is vital in unravelling dark mojo and aiding the rescue of young Yenniku. Recognized among the Darkspear as one of their most powerful practitioners of traditional witchcraft, Kin'weelay commands deep knowledge of spirits, hexes, and soul magic. When matters involving ancestral spirits or hostile troll enchantments arise, Horde scouts in Stranglethorn Vale look to him to pierce the magical veil.

npc:kindal-moonweaver.text: Kindal Moonweaver. Kindal Moonweaver is a night elf secluded within a concealed nook in the craggy mountains of Feralas, just north of the Grimtotem Compound. Deeply troubled by the mistreatment of wildlife in the wilderness, she watches the aggressive tauren tribe below while seeking help to free captured beasts. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, sharing a mission to defend the forest's innocent creatures. Perched upon a narrow, winding mountain path partially hidden behind timber east of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver maintains a secret vigil over the valley below. While much of Feralas is contested between the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas, Kindal focuses on a more localized and immediate cruelty. Down in the hollow, the Grimtotem tribe operates a fortified compound, capturing and penning up local fauna for reasons far from benign. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and undo the suffering inside.
