Kindal's primary concern lies with the sacred balance and gentle creatures of Feralas that cannot defend themselves against brutish captors. Along with her kin, Jer'kai Moonweaver, she seeks the emancipation of caged beasts and looks out for young animals left stranded by violent poaching. Rather than engaging in grand territorial war, her attention is fixed on compassion: freeing caged sprites and finding a home for an orphaned sprite darter.

npc:kirge-sternhorn.text: Kirge Sternhorn. Kirge Sternhorn is a tauren stationed in the rugged frontier of the Barrens. Serving as a steady presence for travelers journeying across central Kalimdor, he directs fledgling Horde adventurers northward toward the vital outpost of the Crossroads. The vast, sun-baked plains of the Barrens are daunting for newly arrived wanderers, and Kirge Sternhorn stands as a helpful guide along their path. Stationed south of the central trails, he watches over travelers moving between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Understanding the dangers of marauding quilboar and fierce predators roaming the savanna, Kirge ensures that young adventurers find their footing and seek out the greater Horde presence gathering to the north.

npc:klannoc-macleod.text: Klannoc Macleod. Klannoc Macleod is a rugged human warrior residing on Fray Island, situated off the eastern shores of the Barrens. Renowned as an arbiter of martial prowess, he tests aspiring brawlers from both the Alliance and the Horde who seek to master combat stances. Those who earn his respect are directed further inland toward greater trials of strength. Isolated on Fray Island off the coast of the Merchant Coast in the Barrens, Klannoc Macleod oversees a brutal proving ground for seasoned fighters. Despite being human, Klannoc stands apart from the typical political squabbles of the Alliance and Horde, judging contenders solely by their grit, blade work, and resolve under fire. Warriors directed to Fray Island are subjected to Macleod's trial: the Affray. Contenders step onto a raised iron grating to endure relentless waves of eager brawlers while Klannoc watches. Those who withstand the onslaught and defeat his chosen champion earn his seal of approval, proving they possess the temperament necessary for berserker training.

npc:kor-ghan.text: Kor'ghan. Kor'ghan is a Darkspear jungle troll who can be found lingering in the murky caverns of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. Positioned right outside Rekkul's Poisons, he seeks assistance in concocting remedies against venomous wilderness predators. Standing before Rekkul's Poisons in the cavernous depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan keeps close watch over remedies and toxins alike. From the capital he dispatches adventurers across the red canyons to gather venomous components from Durotar's scorpids in order to prepare vital antidotes.

npc:korran.text: Korran. Korran is a Darkspear troll researcher stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Serving Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar, he monitors odd happenings across the scrublands and studies the emerging menace of the insectoid silithid. While most at the Crossroads concern themselves with aggressive quilboar and local centaur clans, Korran keeps a watchful eye on subtler, more insidious threats. Stationed on orders from Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar, the troll scout observes the changing land and coordinates the collection of intelligence for the Horde's leadership. Korran's primary concern has shifted south toward the Field of Giants, where strange insectoid creatures known as silithid have begun burrowing into the earth. Disturbed by their aggressive nature and rapid encroachment, he enlists passing adventurers to dig up intact eggs using his claw tool, attempting to decipher where the swarm originated and what danger it poses to the young Horde.

npc:kravel-koalbeard.text: Kravel Koalbeard. Kravel Koalbeard is a scheming dwarven entrepreneur and con artist stationed out at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Rather than cheering purely for the love of the sport, he views the fierce gnome and goblin racing rivalry as a golden opportunity to fill his pockets. From scavenging stray machine parts to fixing race results through blackmail and booze, Kravel is always hunting for his next profitable scheme. While most spectators and crew members at the Mirage Raceway are consumed by mechanical rivalries and the roar of rocket engines, Kravel Koalbeard has his eyes squarely on everyone's coin purses. He is an opportunist who operates in the dusty cracks of the raceway encampment, quick to offer contracts and favors that rarely have clean motives. Kravel sees the high-stakes friction between gnome and goblin engineers not as an inspiring competition, but as a fertile ground for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

npc:kreldig-ungor.text: Kreldig Ungor. Kreldig Ungor is an enterprising dwarven operative representing Reclaimers Inc., stationed high among the crags of Nijel's Point in Desolace. Tasked with managing field operations in the barren wasteland, he hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and secure valuable local reagents. His salvage and recovery contracts make him a central contact for travelers navigating the hostile region. Nijel's Point offers the Alliance a rare sanctuary amid the blighted canyons of Desolace, making it an ideal staging ground for commercial opportunists like Kreldig Ungor. Representing Reclaimers Inc., Kreldig has ventured far from the safety of Khaz Modan into a desolate wilderness contested by centaur clans, demons, and the Horde. Where others see ruin and ash, Kreldig sees untapped profit and lost assets ripe for recovery. A primary venture bringing Kreldig to Desolace involves the lost vessel of Karnitol, which wrecked along the treacherous western coast. Karnitol's shipment held prized goods, and Kreldig orchestrates efforts to track down the debris and retrieve the scattered cargo before scavengers or coastal sea giants can claim it all. Beyond maritime salvage, Kreldig oversees the procurement of Desolace's strange biological and mineral treasures for Reclaimers Inc. The harsh environment breeds unique fauna and flora, whose parts fetch high prices among alchemists and engineers back in the Eastern Kingdoms. Adventurers willing to brave the wasteland's predators find steady pay beneath Kreldig's ledger.

npc:krolg.text: Krolg. Krolg is an uncorrupted furbolg living in an isolated hut south of Mystral Lake in Ashenvale. Formerly a member of the Foulweald tribe, he was cast out by his kin, who fell to demonic madness, and will only speak with those who appear to him in furbolg form. While most of the Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale have succumbed to the demonic taint left behind by the Burning Legion, Krolg remains lucid and untouched by madness. Residing in a secluded shelter south of Mystral Lake, he keeps a cautious vigil over the forest. Having witnessed the tragic descent of his brethren into senseless violence, he refuses to interact with outsiders at face value, speaking only with beings that appear as kin.

npc:krom-stoutarm.text: Krom Stoutarm. Krom Stoutarm is a dwarven scholar and warlock found deep within the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Unlike most of his kin who delve solely into ancient stone and titan relics, Krom studies darker, arcane texts and demonic rituals. He acts as an indispensable contact for Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. The Hall of Explorers is typically known for dwarven archaeologists obsessed with picks, shovels, and titan artifacts. Krom Stoutarm cuts an unusual figure among them. Lurking in the Library surrounded by massive tomes, he pursues occult lore and the binding rites of demonic summoners. His presence in Ironforge demonstrates that while warlock arts are widely distrusted, scholar-practitioners who study the forbidden arts still operate within the mountain city's halls. When Alliance warlocks seek to bind potent demonic servants like the felhunter, their journey inevitably crosses paths with Krom. Possessing knowledge of scattered occult volumes, he directs aspiring summoners far across the seas—including dangerous forays among the centaur of Thousand Needles—to recover torn pages and fragments of the infamous Tome of the Cabal.

npc:krusk.text: Krusk. Krusk is an orc scout stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Dispatched directly under Warchief Thrall's orders to investigate the Syndicate and recover relics from the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he now coordinates reconnaissance and rescue efforts after his initial infiltration was ambushed. When Warchief Thrall turned his attention back to the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he dispatched Krusk and a small strike team to scout Syndicate activity and retrieve relics tied to the fortress's grim past. However, the human outlaws proved more entrenched and coordinated than anticipated. An ambush inside Durnholde's crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scout squad. Krusk managed to fight his way out, but his comrades were taken captive: Drull and Tog'thar were locked away within the ruins, while the expedition's leader, Gol'dir, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Regrouping at Tarren Mill, Krusk now directs Horde adventurers to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and liberate his trapped comrades. Beyond recovering his scouts, Krusk remains fixated on dismantling the Syndicate's hold over Hillsbrad. The fallen nobles of Alterac represent a volatile threat, operating out of Durnholde Keep and scheming against both Horde outposts and their former Alliance brethren. Working from Tarren Mill, Krusk tracks the movements of Syndicate leaders, such as Lord Aliden Perenolde, hoping to sever their leadership before they can threaten the tenuous Horde foothold in Lordaeron.

npc:kuray-bin.text: Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin is a Darkspear jungle troll scout stationed at a guard post outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He watches the surrounding forest trails for night elf scouts sneaking close to the Horde encampment. Positioned just outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin keeps watch against Alliance infiltration in the deep woods of Ashenvale. The Silverwing Sentinels constantly patrol the surrounding canopy, sending agile outrunners across the border to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Knowing that unmonitored scouts quickly become ambushing forces, Kuray'bin directs capable Horde fighters to hunt down the outrunners before they can report back to Silverwing Outpost.

npc:kzan-thornslash.text: Kzan Thornslash. Kzan Thornslash is an orc weapon merchant stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He provides essential starter weaponry and supplies to fresh recruits beginning their training under the Horde. Situated within the dusty red canyon of the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash serves as the primary weapon vendor for young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps as warriors of the Horde. Offering an assortment of basic armaments—ranging from crude hand axes and shortswords to clubs and staves—Kzan ensures that newly awakened aspirants are armed adequately to face the local wildlife and regional hazards.

npc:laird.text: Laird. Laird is a night elf fish vendor found inside the seaside inn of Auberdine. Working along Darkshore's mist-shrouded coast, he provides trade goods and culinary recipes to travelers and fishermen braving the rugged shoreline. Situated inside the bustling inn of Auberdine, Laird sells fresh fish and supplies to sailors, locals, and journeying adventurers. Darkshore's waters are notoriously turbulent and rife with danger compared to the sheltered shores of Teldrassil, but Laird knows well that risk brings reward. For daring anglers willing to cast their lines along the misty beaches, the local catch yields a handsome profit. Laird remains closely connected to fishing operations across the channel in Teldrassil. He serves as an essential contact for courier runs between the island boughs of Rut'theran Village and the mainland port, receiving shipments from his fellow fisher Nessa Shadowsong and ensuring the lines of coastal commerce stay open.

npc:lakota-windsong.text: Lakota Windsong. Lakota Windsong is a young tauren held captive atop the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. After rejecting an unwanted proposal from Arnak Grimtotem, she was abducted by force and awaits rescue from the Grimtotem tribe's clutches. Not long after the Third War, Lakota Windsong was pursued by Arnak Grimtotem. Unwilling to join his clan or accept his courtship, she turned down his proposal. Arnak refused to take no for an answer; he returned under cover of night, slaughtered Lakota's brother when he tried to intervene, and carried her off into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Confined high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, she remains trapped under heavy guard while Arnak still insists on making her his bride.

npc:lanka-farshot.text: Lanka Farshot. Lanka Farshot is a tauren hunter trainer stationed at Camp Narache within the Red Cloud Mesa. He guides novice tauren hunters as they take their first steps in tracking, marksmanship, and surviving the plains of Mulgore. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot greets new tauren called to the path of the hunter. Fresh recruits arrive carrying an etched note directing them to seek his counsel. Under his steady eye, apprentices learn the fundamentals of ranged combat, tracking prey, and respecting the wild beasts that roam the grassy plains of Mulgore. His teachings ensure that every young hunter serves as a capable scout and provider for the tribe.

npc:lar-prowltusk.text: Lar Prowltusk. Lar Prowltusk is a Darkspear troll sentinel stationed southwest of Sen'jin Village in Durotar. From his post on the frontier, he keeps watch over encroaching threats to the young troll settlement, directing adventurers to blunt the advances of nearby enemies. Situated southwest of Sen'jin Village along the rugged Durotar coastline, Lar Prowltusk stands as one of the Darkspear tribe's forward sentinels. With the trolls still working to secure a permanent home after fleeing their sunken island chain, Sen'jin Village faces constant harassment from hostile neighbors. Lar coordinates scouts and warriors to monitor coastal movements and curb the aggression of hostile forces—particularly the Kolkar centaur—ensuring the fragile settlement has room to breathe.

npc:laris-geardawdle.text: Laris Geardawdle. Laris Geardawdle is an eccentric gnomish researcher stationed in the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. He dedicates his academic life to studying the bizarre nature and origins of oozes across Azeroth. Adventurers willing to collect noxious slime samples find him an eager, if slightly unhinged, patron. Tucked away among the towering bookshelves and ancient relics of the Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle pursues a rather unglamorous niche of natural philosophy: the genesis of oozes. While his dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings, Laris is convinced that Azeroth's vile, gelatinous horrors hold fascinating alchemical and biological secrets. He tasks roving explorers with gathering caustic samples from remote corners of the world, eager to test his strange hypotheses on how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

npc:lars.text: Lars. Lars is a beleaguered human survivor camping out in the wilderness of Duskwood. Along with his companion Sven Yorgen, he struggles to hold his ground on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank against the terrors that stalk the forest. Perched in a modest camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars ekes out a precarious survival far from the questionable safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is treacherous at the best of times, but the surrounding woods crawl with ferocious beasts, relentless undead, and creeping worgen. Lars stays close by Sven Yorgen, striving simply to stay alive in an increasingly hostile wilderness. Survival at the camp requires constant vigilance against the local predators. Lars finds himself sorely pressed by the relentless packs of starving dire wolves that haunt the shadows around their fire. Unable to lower his guard or drive them back alone, he relies on capable travelers to thin the hungry predators before his small camp is completely overrun.

npc:lelanai.text: Lelanai. Lelanai is a night elf mount handler residing in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus. She provides the fierce saber mounts of the night elves to worthy riders, offering both standard nightsabers and swift war beasts to her kin and trusted allies of Darnassus. Stationed beside riding instructor Jartsam among the towering trees of the Cenarion Enclave, Lelanai attends to some of the finest big cats bred in Kalimdor. Night elves have long formed profound bonds with the fierce predators of northern forests, training nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged terrain with predator grace. Lelanai serves as the primary provider of these revered mounts in the capital. While saber mounts are freely offered to any night elf of appropriate skill, outsiders face a much stricter threshold. Given the sacred nature of the cats and the natural aloofness of the kaldorei, Lelanai will not entrust a beast to non-night elf adventurers unless they have earned the highest degree of respect and renown with the city of Darnassus.

npc:lieutenant-haggerdin.text: Lieutenant Haggerdin. Lieutenant Haggerdin is a dwarven officer stationed upon the Headland in the Alterac Mountains. Standing watch outside the fortified gate to Alterac Valley, he acts as the primary recruitment and liaison officer for the Stormpike Guard. He evaluates aspiring Alliance champions and rewards those who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. Perched in the snowy heights of the Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the muster point for the Alliance's ongoing campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners flutter beside the massive wooden gate as recruits and veterans assemble under his watchful eye, preparing to plunge into the frigid warzone. Serving the Stormpike Expedition, Haggerdin ensures that only tested warriors represent Ironforge and the Grand Alliance in the valley. Through challenges like the Proving Grounds, he tasks recruits with recovering banners and relics, and bestows official commendations, insignias, and rank recognitions as soldiers rise through the ranks of the Stormpike Guard.

npc:lieutenant-lisande.text: Lieutenant Lisande. Lieutenant Lisande is an emissary of the Argent Dawn stationed upon the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. As a human operating openly in tauren lands, she serves as a liaison against the shared existential threat of the Scourge. While human faces are rare across the windblown heights of Thunder Bluff, the Argent Dawn transcends traditional faction enmities. Lieutenant Lisande serves the holy order by watching for signs of the Lich King's taint even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, she rallies brave Horde champions to ride out and investigate the encroaching menace before it can defile the sacred earth.

npc:lieutenant-nevell.text: Lieutenant Nevell. Lieutenant Nevell is an officer of the Argent Dawn stationed outside the gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Serving as a bulwark against the spreading darkness of the Scourge, he coordinates local defenders and alerts arriving adventurers to undead threats probing the dwarf kingdom's borders. While the Argent Dawn is most renowned for holding the line in the shattered Plaguelands of Lordaeron, its vigilance reaches far into the south. Stationed in the freezing winds outside Ironforge, Lieutenant Nevell represents the order's proactive defense against necromantic incursions. When Scourge activity stirs in the mountain passes of Dun Morogh, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front lines to ensure Ironforge's snowy doorstep remains secure.

npc:lieutenant-orrin.text: Lieutenant Orrin. Lieutenant Orrin is an officer of the Argent Dawn stationed at the gates of Stormwind City. Positioned in the Valley of Heroes, he coordinates local defense against incursions by the Scourge and directs fresh recruits to investigate undead threats outside the capital's walls. While the Argent Dawn is primarily known for holding the front lines in the ruined north, their presence extends south to safeguard vital strongholds like Stormwind City. Lieutenant Orrin stands near the towering statues of the Valley of Heroes, watching the road for signs of corruption. When necromantic magic stirs outside the capital, he is tasked with sounding the alarm and rallying adventurers before foul forces can threaten the populace. Orrin acts as a primary liaison between the independent order and volunteers within the southern kingdom. When signs of the Scourge surface beyond the city gates, he marshals able-bodied scouts and sends them out to gather intelligence and secure hazardous artifacts, such as cracked necrotic crystals, to better understand and repel the undead threat.

npc:loganaar.text: Loganaar. Loganaar is a night elf druidic instructor residing in the haven of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Dedicated to guiding initiates from both the Alliance and the Horde, he instructs young druids as they attune to the wild and prepare for the call of the Emerald Dream. Situated amidst the serene boughs of Nighthaven, Loganaar serves as a primary mentor to newly initiated druids traveling to Moonglade. Regardless of whether an initiate hails from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, Loganaar provides guidance in balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. He reminds his students that even within cold stone and unfamiliar lands, true tranquility must be found within oneself. He also acts as a welcoming guide for those journeying deeper into the Cenarion Circle's affairs, sending promising students to wanderers like Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater or deeper into ancient woodland rites. Beyond fundamental spellcraft, Loganaar prepares students for the ultimate destiny shared by Kalimdor's traditional protectors: the deep slumber of the Emerald Dream. He instructs initiates on the sacred connection between Azeroth's primal spirit realm and the waking world, reminding them that true mastery will one day require hibernating for centuries to walk among nature's purest, unblemished forms under the guidance of the demigods.

npc:lomac-gearstrip.text: Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac Gearstrip is an ambitious gnome inventor based in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned for formulating the devastating NG-5 explosive, he liaises with fellow gnomish researchers operating across Kalimdor. Amid the clanging gears and hissing pipes of Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues the finer points of gnomish ordnance. Like many exiled gnomes who fled the tragedy at Gnomeregan, Lomac has integrated his tinkering operations directly into the dwarven capital. His workshop focuses on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions designed to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds. Lomac's proudest contribution to modern combat engineering is the NG-5 explosive. Formulated for maximum destructive yield, the compound demands precise handling and rare chemical reagents. To refine and deploy such hazardous inventions in the field, Lomac maintains contact with old colleagues stationed in distant theaters, exchanging technical orders and dangerous supplies across the Great Sea.

npc:longbraid-the-grim.text: Longbraid the Grim. Longbraid the Grim is an Ironforge dwarf commander stationed just outside the fallen fortress of Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands. Mourning the loss of his brother and the overrun of the Thandol Span, he coordinates the surviving dwarf forces against the invading Dark Iron clan. Positioned within sight of the bridge to the Arathi Highlands, Longbraid the Grim rallies what remains of the dwarven garrison after the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr. The sudden assault devastated the regional defenders and resulted in the death of Longbraid's own brother during the siege of the Thandol Span. Burdened by grief and hatred, Longbraid refuses to abandon the northern boundary, directing travelers and surviving mountaineers in surgical strikes to curb the Dark Iron advance. Beyond defending the approach to the bridge, Longbraid oversees broader dwarven operations across the Wetlands. He dispatched vital soldiers to escort Prospector Whelgar into the marshlands and works relentlessly to reclaim the lost fortifications of Dun Modr, vowing retribution against the Dark Iron saboteurs.

npc:loramus-thalipedes.text: Loramus Thalipedes. Loramus Thalipedes is a reclusive night elf demon hunter secluded on a remote isle off the coast of Azshara. Flanked by loyal felhounds, he dedicates his existence to destroying Razelikh the Defiler, directing seasoned champions through rituals to strike down the dreadlord. Perched on a solitary, storm-tossed island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes stands apart from the rest of his kin. He is a demon hunter—an exile who underwent the agonizing ritual of blinding himself to gain spectral sight. Surrounded by three towering felhounds named Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, Loramus watches the unseen currents of demonic corruption across Azeroth while keeping a watchful vigil over the shattered ruins of Azshara.

npc:lord-arkkoroc.text: Lord Arkkoroc. Lord Arkkoroc is an ancient, towering sea giant who dwells within the ruined Temple of Arkkoran along the ragged coast of Azshara. Described by the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes as a lesser deity, he holds sway over the surrounding waters and commands lesser sea giants who serve as his sons. Reclining amidst the brine-crusted ruins of the Temple of Arkkoran, Lord Arkkoroc is far more than a typical sea giant. To hermits like Loramus Thalipedes, this colossal being is considered a lesser deity whose divine will shapes the surrounding waters. His sons patrol the crags and shallows around the sanctuary, enforcing his quiet dominion over Azshara's tempestuous shores.

npc:lord-baurles-k-wishock.text: Lord Baurles K. Wishock. Lord Baurles K. Wishock is a nobleman residing in Stormwind Keep's Petitioner's Chamber. Known among barkeeps for his unpaid tabs and fondness for strong drink, he stumbled upon darker dealings than mere drunkenness in the city's underbelly. Holding court among the petitioners and dignitaries within Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock is a member of the influential House of Nobles. Despite his elevated station, Wishock developed a habit of frequenting the dive bars of the Mage Quarter, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, leaving behind substantial unpaid bills. While drinking there, however, he caught wind of the warlock coven practicing dark arts in the cellars beneath the floorboards. Determined to shut the tavern down, Wishock began petitioning fellow nobles for a formal investigation—unaware that uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

npc:lord-grayson-shadowbreaker.text: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker is a veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. One of the Alliance's foremost paladins, he trains budding champions of the Light and oversees the sacred, arduous trials required for senior paladins to claim their holy chargers. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker stands among the foremost defenders of the Alliance, anchoring the order's presence in Stormwind City. A veteran of the Silver Hand, Grayson does not merely instruct recruits in martial skill; he tests their spiritual conviction. When promising knights demonstrate their readiness, Grayson dispatches them north toward the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands to aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

npc:lord-jorach-ravenholdt.text: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is the master of Ravenholdt, an elite guild of rogues and assassins operating out of a secluded estate in the Alterac Mountains. He directs the league's clandestine operations, training promising operatives while waging a bitter war against the regional bandits of the Syndicate. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over the Assassin's League from his hidden manor nestled in the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he opens his halls to outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins regardless of allegiance, provided they exhibit exceptional skill and respect his authority. Under his command, the league acts as both a fraternity for master thieves and an independent syndicate for wetwork and espionage. Ravenholdt harbors a fierce hatred for the Syndicate—the band of disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws—and routinely directs his subordinates and visiting freelancers to sabotage their camps and plunder their assets.

npc:lord-maxwell-tyrosus.text: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus is the supreme commander of the Argent Dawn, stationed at their forward redoubt of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand from the Third War, he guides the coalition's crusade against the Scourge and orchestrates strikes into blighted strongholds like Stratholme. Maxwell Tyrosus rode alongside Uther the Lightbringer during the catastrophic Third War, guarding the exits of Andorhal when the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After the fall of Lordaeron, he cast his lot with the Argent Dawn, an order that welcomes anyone willing to stand against the Scourge, in stark contrast to the human-only zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade. Tyrosus now leads the Argent Dawn and oversees the defenses of Light's Hope Chapel. From his command post within the chapel, he oversees broad military operations across the Plaguelands, including tactical assaults led by Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff against Baron Rivendare inside the ruins of Stratholme.

npc:lord-shalzaru.text: Lord Shalzaru. Lord Shalzaru is the tyrannical leader of the Hatecrest naga operating out of the Isle of Dread off the coast of Feralas. Ruling his serpentine followers with absolute cruelty, he oversees extensive excavations among the submerged and ruined elven settlements. His recent discovery of a strange, ancient relic has drawn the attention of outside investigators eager to wrest it from his grasp. Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga, directing their presence along the southern coast of Feralas. From his subterranean lair within a cavern on the Isle of Dread, he enforces his rule through cruelty and ruthless authority. Under his command, the Hatecrest scour the ancient ruins of ancient Kalimdor, searching for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left behind from the Sundering. During excavations south of the primary ruins across the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru personally uncovered a strange, ancient relic. The purpose and power of this artifact remain a mystery, but its recovery by such a powerful naga warlord presents a clear threat. Operatives on the mainland seek brave champions to venture into the serpent's den, end Shalzaru's command, and secure the odd relic before the Hatecrest can turn it to darker ends.

npc:lorekeeper-raintotem.text: Lorekeeper Raintotem. Lorekeeper Raintotem is a tauren elder stationed in northern Mulgore just south of Red Rocks. He tends to the sacred burial grounds and asks adventurers to drive off the Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Positioned near the sacred bluffs of Red Rocks in Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends to the spiritual obligations of his people. He asks adventurers to drive Bristleback Interlopers from the burial ground, restoring peace to the ancestors' resting place. Beyond testing fledgling heroes, Lorekeeper Raintotem watches over the hallowed burial sites at Red Rocks. When Bristleback quilboar interlopers disturb the sanctified resting places of deceased tauren chieftains and shamans, Raintotem enlists travelers to restore dignity and quiet the disturbed dead.

npc:loslor-rudge.text: Loslor Rudge. Loslor Rudge is an enterprising dwarven engineering supplier stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. He provides mechanical parts, tools, and munitions to tinkerers across the snowy mountain ridges, keeping critical connections open with gunsmiths like Hegnar Rumbleshot. Operating out of Steelgrill's Depot just down the road from Kharanos, Loslor Rudge keeps a steady inventory of engineering essentials—ranging from copper modulators and bronze tubing to blasting powder and spanners. Dun Morogh's harsh weather and sprawling tinker operations mean practical parts are constantly in demand, and Loslor prides himself on keeping the local gearheads supplied. However, the wilderness between outposts is treacherous; when a courier taking a shortcut near the Grizzled Den was chased away by wendigos, an essential shipment of ammunition meant for his valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot, was left behind in the snow.

npc:lotwil-veriatus.text: Lotwil Veriatus. Lotwil Veriatus is an eccentric gnomish scholar conducting dangerous elemental experiments in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. Stationed east of Kargath with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and a mechanical attendant named Servo, he is dedicated to blending arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering into a unified discipline. Originally from Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil envisions a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes these three disciplines should not be practiced in isolation, but harmonized. In pursuit of this dream, he chose the harsh Badlands as his laboratory to study native rock elementals and construct binding shackles capable of mastering elemental forces. While an accomplished researcher—having studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs in the past—his single-minded focus often blinds him to the explosive hazards of his fieldwork.

npc:lucius.text: Lucius. Lucius is a dwarf operative found near the docks of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Operating as an undercover field contact for Stormwind's SI:7 intelligence service, he assists operatives with specialized reconnaissance and trade skills. While Lucius presents himself casually on the Lakeshire waterfront, he is in fact a clandestine operative tied directly to Stormwind's intelligence apparatus, SI:7. From his post on the docks, he monitors trade, unusual traffic, and regional threats encroaching on Redridge. Operatives dispatched eastward from Stormwind are directed to him to coordinate covert tasks and hone practical fieldwork arts such as lockpicking, ensuring the Crown maintains hidden reach far beyond Elwynn Forest.

npc:lyria-du-lac.text: Lyria Du Lac. Lyria Du Lac is a human warrior trainer stationed in Goldshire within Elwynn Forest. Tucked away just behind the village smithy, she drills novice combatants and guides young warriors as they begin mastering their stances and arms. While Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn bustles with travellers and its blacksmith hammers away at local trade goods, Lyria Du Lac keeps to the yard behind the forge. Experienced in martial discipline, she serves the Alliance by instructing fledgeling warriors fresh from Northshire Abbey. She evaluates their readiness and introduces them to specialized combat techniques, ensuring that those who take up shield and blade for Stormwind can hold their own against the encroaching threats of Elwynn Forest.

npc:ma-stonefield.text: Ma Stonefield. Ma Stonefield is a human matriarch residing at the Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn Forest. Standing right outside the family homestead alongside Auntie Bernice, she deals with the daily hardships of rural farm life amidst neighboring rivalries and pest troubles. Standing beside her family cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest, Ma Stonefield watches over the farmstead alongside "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. Life between the neighboring Maclure homestead and the nearby pumpkin patches is rarely peaceful. Local wild boars continuously threaten the family crops, and none poses a greater nuisance than Princess, an enormous prize sow notorious for trampling fields and devouring hard-earned harvests.

npc:magga.text: Magga. Magga is an orc resident living in the Valley of Trials within Durotar. Stationed near the Den, she serves as a welcoming face for newly arrived Horde adventurers beginning their journey in the valley. The Valley of Trials is the first taste of the world for young orcs and darkspear trolls. Positioned near the Den, Magga greets new arrivals to the valley. While she keeps a low profile among the valley's busy trainers and recruits, she helps bind the small camp together.

npc:magis-sparkmantle.text: Magis Sparkmantle. Magis Sparkmantle is a gnome mage trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. He offers guidance and training to fledgling spellcasters who venture out from Coldridge Valley into the heart of Dun Morogh. While dwarves gather in the Thunderbrew Distillery for hearty ales, Magis Sparkmantle provides an arcane presence among the casks and kegs of Kharanos. Gnome mages often integrate closely with their dwarven allies across Dun Morogh, and Sparkmantle serves as a key mentor for novice spellcasters ready to expand their theoretical and practical grasp of the arcane arts. Beyond instructing novices in basic incantations, Magis ensures that promising students connect with broader magical circles. When mages outgrow early local instruction or require specialized guidance, Sparkmantle directs them further afield, sending them toward fellow practitioners like Bink or mentors stationed across the Alliance's primary hubs.

npc:magistrate-henry-maleb.text: Magistrate Henry Maleb. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees civic administration in the port town of Southshore, the Alliance's primary coastal bastion in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining order amid constant threats, he focuses much of his authority on hunting down the Syndicate conspirators targeting the town's leadership. Operating from the town hall in Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb handles civil governance for one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. The town sits under constant siege from the Forsaken to the north and West, while ruthless highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb stepped into his current station after the mysterious assassination of the prior magistrate, an act he attributes directly to the Syndicate. Determined not to suffer the same fate, he coordinates active investigations to root out hidden assassins, dismantle Syndicate supply networks, and unmask the rogue nobles pulling the strings from the ruins of Alterac.

npc:magus-rimtori.text: Magus Rimtori. Magus Rimtori is a rogue blood elf sorceress leading an expedition among the ancient ruins of Azshara. Known for her ruthless deception, she manipulated the Horde into securing her passage across Kalimdor before butchering her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori led an expedition of high-borne blood elves across the sea to the ancient shores of Azshara. To ensure her party survived the perils of Kalimdor, she manipulated the orc Belgrom, charming and playing him until he agreed to supply an armed escort. Once the soldiers had delivered her safely to her destination, Rimtori revealed her true colors, turning on her protectors and massacring the entire garrison. Establishing her forces at the Thalassian Base Camp, she ventured out into the coastal wilds accompanied by elite bodyguards to hunt for forgotten magical artifacts.

npc:mai-ah.text: Mai'ah. Mai'ah is a jungle troll mage trainer stationed within the sun-scorched basin of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. She mentors fledgling spellcasters among the Darkspear trolls who step into the red canyons to hone their command of the arcane. For young trolls beginning the path of wizardry, she offers early guidance and instruction in the foundational arts of magic. While orcs overwhelmingly favor the primal call of the elements or the physical dominance of the warrior, Darkspear trolls possess a rare affinity for arcane study. Standing within the Valley of Trials, Mai'ah serves as an instructor for young troll mages arriving to undertake their rites of adulthood. She receives candidates carrying glyphic inscriptions and begins shaping their chaotic raw power into disciplined incantations, ensuring they learn the control required to survive Durotar's perils.

npc:major-mattingly.text: Major Mattingly. Major Mattingly is a seasoned officer of the Stormwind Army stationed at the grand gates in the Valley of Heroes. Serving under General Marcus Jonathan, he assists in safeguarding the capital's main entrance and advising capable crafters on protecting heroes against draconic threats. Standing watch in the Valley of Heroes, Major Mattingly is one of the high-ranking officers directly responsible for Stormwind City's primary landward defense. A grizzled veteran soldier whose face bears the lines of hard-won experience, he serves under General Marcus Jonathan alongside the city's standing garrison. Beyond his daily duties overseeing gate patrols and incoming travelers, Mattingly possesses specialized tactical knowledge regarding the lethal nature of dragons. He is recognized by seasoned adventurers as a vital contact when learning to craft protective dragonscale gear necessary for braving the realm's deadliest lairs.

npc:major-samuelson.text: Major Samuelson. Major Samuelson is a high-ranking officer in the Stormwind City Guard stationed within the throne room of Stormwind Keep. As an experienced military commander, he oversees vital personnel matters and previously mentored junior officers such as Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Standing within Stormwind Keep before the royal court, Major Samuelson represents the leadership of the Stormwind City Guard. He oversees officer postings and administrative military orders across the realm. Notably, he mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, an officer stationed far north at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. When junior commanders find themselves overwhelmed or seeking transfer from distant frontier garrisons, their requests and official reports travel directly across the kingdom to Major Samuelson's desk in the capital.

npc:mankrik.text: Mankrik. Mankrik is a grief-stricken orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. After a vicious quilboar ambush separated him from his wife, Olgra, he has dedicated his life to avenging her and cutting down every bristled beast he can find. While traveling through the scrublands of the Barrens, Mankrik and his wife Olgra were overrun by swarms of quilboar during a skirmish at a small tauren settlement. Separated in the chaos and frantic fighting, Mankrik watched Olgra disappear under a tide of tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Overwhelmed by fury, he fought recklessly until he was struck down unconscious. He survived only because a passing tauren druid discovered him bleeding out along the Gold Road and bound his injuries. Recovering at the Crossroads, Mankrik found himself paralyzed by grief and an all-consuming bloodlust. Though local leaders like Thork warn that his blind hatred clouds his judgment and refuse to mount official war parties, Mankrik refuses to move on. Haunted by uncertainty over Olgra's fate, he enlists any willing Horde travelers to scour the Barrens for sign of his lost mate and to slaughter any quilboar that cross their path.

npc:marcus-redpath.text: Marcus Redpath. Marshal Marcus Redpath is the senior military authority defending the Alliance town of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He organizes patrols and bounty contracts to hold off surrounding ogres, murlocs, and naga. His leadership is essential to maintaining Lordaeron's last southern bastion on the coast. Marcus Redpath is the marshal of Southshore, the Alliance port on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Southshore endured the fall of Lordaeron's capital and the devastating Scourge invasion, and Redpath now stands at the head of its defense, guarding the port's beleaguered survivors. In the wake of the Third War, Southshore stands virtually alone against hostile forces pressing in from every side. Marshal Redpath coordinates defense operations across the Hillsbrad Foothills, enlisting seasoned adventurers to push back the Crushridge ogres creeping down from Alterac and purge dangerous naga and murloc encampments along the coastline. With the Forsaken occupying the north and Tarren Mill heavily fortified nearby, Redpath's vigilance is one of the few barriers preventing the regional Alliance presence from collapsing entirely.

npc:mardant-strongoak.text: Mardant Strongoak. Mardant Strongoak is a night elf druid trainer residing in Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil. He guides fledgling druids in communing with the spirits of nature and introduces them to the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, young night elves who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. His primary task is teaching novitiates how to open their senses to nature spirits, interpret their murmurs, and channel rejuvenating magics. For those taking their initial steps as protectors of the wild, he is often the first master to unveil the vast complexities and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

npc:marek-ironheart.text: Marek Ironheart. Marek Ironheart is a veteran dwarven hunter stationed at the Farstrider Lodge in south-eastern Loch Modan. Dedicated to the traditions of the wild, he tests wandering travelers and marksmen alike before welcoming them into the ranks of the lodge's honored hunters. Perched on the scenic ridge overlooking the lake, the Farstrider Lodge serves as an outpost for the finest marksmen and trackers in the dwarven lands. Marek Ironheart embodies this frontier spirit. Unimpressed by titles or talk, Marek requires anyone seeking the lodge's respect to demonstrate their practical prowess against the varied beasts roaming Loch Modan, proving they have the patience and nerve demanded of a true stalker of the wild.

npc:marisa-du-paige.text: Marisa du'Paige. Marisa du'Paige is a rare human rogue spellcaster found lurking within the sprawling cave network outside the entrance to the Deadmines in southwestern Westfall. Aligned with the outlaws operating beneath Moonbrook, she wields arcane magic alongside the laborers and highwaymen guarding the tunnels. Deep inside the winding caverns that lead toward the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, most defenders are rough-hewn cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs. Marisa du'Paige stands out among them as a skilled human mage. While most spellcasters of the kingdom train within the sanctioned halls of Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, du'Paige has cast her lot with the outlaws and brigands hiding in Westfall's subterranean depths.

npc:marleth-barleybrew.text: Marleth Barleybrew. Marleth Barleybrew is an ambitious dwarven brewer stationed out in Brewnall Village. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan's dominance over the local beer market, she constantly schemes to prove her family's brew is superior to Kharanos's famous Thunder Ale. In Dun Morogh, alcohol is taken as seriously as steel, and the rivalry between the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families is legendary. Marleth Barleybrew resents the near-monopoly that Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin maintain out of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Convinced her own craft is every bit as robust, she seeks clever ways to slip Barleybrew kegs into the hands of tavern patrons. Rather than engaging in open conflict, she opts for petty subterfuge, recruiting passing travelers to secretly swap out Kharanos's prized ale casks with her own.

npc:marryk-nurribit.text: Marryk Nurribit. Marryk Nurribit is the resident gnome mage trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A bit more fond of local brews than disciplined pedagogy, he introduces fledgling gnomish arcanists to their craft while frequently soliciting spare coins for a drink. Tucked away inside the warm hearth of Anvilmar, Marryk Nurribit offers arcane guidance to young gnomes taking their very first steps into magic. Though knowledgeable in the arcane arts, his demeanor is decidedly casual—often seeming far more interested in nursing a flagon of dwarven ale and bumming spare pocket change off his new pupils than drilling them in complex theorems. Despite his vices, Marryk remains acutely aware of the perils outside Coldridge Valley, regularly warning aspiring spellcasters about the lingering radioactive and trogg-infested horrors of fallen Gnomeregan.

npc:marshal-maxwell.text: Marshal Maxwell. Marshal Maxwell is a high-ranking officer of the Stormwind army stationed at Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Tasked with holding the Alliance's northernmost fortified ridge above the Redridge Mountains against the Blackrock clan and the Dark Iron dwarves, he directs scouting missions into the hostile crags below. He also plays a crucial role in coordinating efforts to discover the fate of his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Morgan's Vigil stands as a precarious outpost on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes, overlooking a wasteland choked with ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Marshal Maxwell commands the Stormwind military detachment stationed here, providing a rare friendly sight for travelers braving the fiery crags. From this rocky bastion, he oversees defensive maneuvers to keep the hostile forces of the mountain contained before they can sweep southward into Redridge and Elwynn.

npc:martie-jainrose.text: Martie Jainrose. Martie Jainrose is Lakeshire's local herbalist, tending to her garden along the edge of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Beside cultivating remedies and flowers for the beleaguered town, she contends with wild beasts trampling her plots and harbors a quiet affection for Guard Parker. Residing in Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose works diligently as the settlement's resident herbalist. Even as Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the region, Martie focuses on keeping the town supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Her daily labors are often disrupted by local wildlife—most notably the monstrous boar Bellygrub, who frequently ravages her prized garden beds. Beyond her herbal pursuits, Martie seems to hold a fondness for Guard Parker, though Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

npc:marukai.text: Marukai. Marukai is a Darkspear jungle troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the foggy coast of northwest Ashenvale. Dedicated to holding this remote beachhead for the Horde, she coordinates efforts to cull the encroaching Wrathtail naga who threaten the outpost. Zoram'gar Outpost sits isolated on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory, and the restless sea. As the Wrathtail naga emerge in force from the waters and ancient elven ruins to claim the shoreline, Marukai works to keep the encampment from being overwhelmed. She directs Horde champions to push the serpent-folk back into the tide and collect their heads, ensuring the outpost remains a viable coastal stronghold.

npc:master-apothecary-lydon.text: Apothecary Lydon. Apothecary Lydon is a morbid researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Tarren Mill. Chronically depressed and intensely bored, he finds joy only in refining lethal concoctions and watching the living suffer. He spearheads the research into potent new toxins aimed at securing Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and furthering Sylvanas's New Plague. Stationed inside the chapel turned laboratory of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon represents the cold, calculating ethos of the Royal Apothecary Society. He is afflicted by a profound, languid melancholy, disgusted by the blooming flowers and crisp air of Hillsbrad Foothills. The only diversion that lifts his perpetual gloom is the art of deathcraft. When left unattended, he passes the time poisoning, dissecting, and reanimating his unfortunate pet frog, Umpi, repeatedly waiting for new reagents to arrive.

npc:master-vornal.text: Master Vornal. Master Vornal is an elderly Darkspear jungle troll who resides in Sen'jin Village along the southern coast of Durotar. Despite his advancing years and extensive knowledge of alchemical concoctions, he stubbornly refuses to take on any apprentices. Master Vornal is a fixture of Sen'jin Village, known for brewing potent draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls. Though age is visibly catching up with him, Vornal remains intensely independent and stubbornly refuses to train any apprentices, preferring to mix his remedies and volatile mixtures entirely by his own hand. Vornal occasionally tasks young adventurers with gathering harsh or peculiar ingredients from the surrounding lands, such as potent materials needed for solvents and mixtures. While he is willing to reward those who assist him, he keeps his precise methods and recipes guarded, treating his craft as a solitary pursuit.

npc:mastok-wrilehiss.text: Mastok Wrilehiss. Mastok Wrilehiss is an orc officer stationed at Splintertree Post in eastern Ashenvale. Serving as a crucial defensive coordinator for the Horde in the contested forest, he directs scouts and warriors to secure nearby borders and handle corrupting elemental threats. His presence is vital for maintaining the precarious foothold the Horde holds amidst constant night elf hostility. Splintertree Post stands deep in the shadow of Ashenvale's towering canopy, completely surrounded by hostile night elven territory. Mastok Wrilehiss serves as one of the post's core defenders, monitoring supply routes and forest activity. The position is perilous; any sign of weakness invites swift strikes from the Sentinels who view the settlement as a despoiling intrusion. From his vantage within the stockade, Mastok actively tasks passing adventurers with critical strategic duties. He keeps watchful eyes on the borders leading into neighboring territories like the Stonetalon Mountains and dispatches scouts to consult shamans such as Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring at Zoram'gar Strand. His duties bridge military defense with monitoring the strange, corrupting forces afflicting the local elementals.

npc:mathredis-firestar.text: Mathredis Firestar. Mathredis Firestar is an eccentric blood elf mage residing at Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He crafts powerful enchantments known as Lesser Arcanums, drawing upon the arcane research of his deceased master. In doing so, he feeds on the residual energies unleashed during the binding process to stave off his magic addiction. Mathredis Firestar learned the craft of making arcanums—concentrated gems of arcane empowerment—from his mentor, Telmius Dreamseeker. Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself. Adventurers who bring Mathredis the proper tomes—such as the Librams of Constitution, Resilience, Rumination, Tenacity, or Voracity—along with rare reagents will find him eager to trade his craft. The process binds volatile magical reagents directly to the text, concentrating their essence into an arcanum that can permanently enchant headwear or leg armor. So long as adventurers supply the components, Mathredis receives both payment and the ambient arcane sustenance he desperately craves.

npc:maur-grimtotem.text: Maur Grimtotem. Maur Grimtotem was an emissary sent by Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem into the depths of Ragefire Chasm. Dispatched on an ill-fated diplomatic mission to the troggs infesting the subterranean tunnels beneath Orgrimmar, he met a brutal end at their hands. Today, only his remains and personal satchel linger in the dark as evidence of the foolish errand. While most in the Horde view troggs as mindless, savage brutes beneath negotiation, Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought otherwise—or at least claimed to. She dispatched Maur Grimtotem deep into the winding caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar to attempt a peaceful overture with the subterranean beasts. Predictably, diplomacy failed. Maur was swiftly slain, his corpse left in the caverns under the watchful eye of the trogg chieftain Oggleflint.

npc:maur-raincaller.text: Maur Raincaller. Maur Raincaller is a tauren resident found residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Connected to the natural and spiritual life of the plains, he assists the village elders and watches over local matters affecting the herds and wild beasts. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village on the shores of Lake Stonebull, Maur Raincaller serves his community by attending to regional ecological and beast-related concerns. Like many who bear the mantle of Raincaller, he pays close attention to the balance of the elements and wildlife across the fertile plains of Mulgore. After a bite from the fearsome strider Mazzranache left his wound infected, Maur turns to capable young travelers to gather the animal parts he needs for a remedy.

npc:maurin-bonesplitter.text: Maurin Bonesplitter. Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings. While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it. Maurin directs most of his malice toward the Burning Blade cult entrenched across Desolace. He harbors utter disgust for their reckless ambition, mocking the cultists for failing to understand that their borrowed power merely binds them as thralls to their demonic masters. Through scrying spells and ritual knowledge, Maurin enlists Horde adventurers to systematically disrupt the cult's summonings and undermine their operations across the barren landscape.

npc:maxan-anvol.text: Maxan Anvol. Maxan Anvol is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Dedicated to the Holy Light, he guides fledgling dwarven priests as they learn to channel divine power amid Dun Morogh's frigid climes. He tests young acolytes to ensure they are worthy of wearing the vestments of the church. While it might seem strange to find an ordained minister of the Holy Light stationed inside Thunderbrew Distillery, it suits dwarven culture well. Kharanos serves as the primary hub between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge, and the local inn is where travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes naturally gather. Maxan tends to the spiritual welfare of the hamlet alongside pints of stout, offering prayers and counsel to any who step through the doors. Maxan Anvol is responsible for vetting novice priests before they venture into the wider world. He tasks initiates with demonstrating mastery over fundamental curative prayers on wounded defenders of Dun Morogh. Those who prove their devotion and practical competence are bestowed their first proper priestly vestments, formally marking their recognized standing within the Church of the Holy Light.

npc:maybell-maclure.text: Maybell Maclure. Maybell Maclure is a young woman living at the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest. Despite a bitter, long-standing feud between her family and the neighboring Stonefields, she has secretly fallen in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield. Life on the Maclure Vineyards is defined by endless labor and an enduring grudge against the neighboring Stonefield family. Caught in the middle is Maybell Maclure, who has fallen deeply in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield, the young heir to the rival farmstead. Kept apart by vigilant relatives and ancient family resentment, Maybell is desperate for any chance to communicate with Tommy Joe beyond the prying eyes of her kin.

npc:melithar-staghelm.text: Melithar Staghelm. Melithar Staghelm is a night elf stationed just outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Teldrassil's starting glade. He assists young night elf adventurers as they embark on their early training, sending them to learn what has brought the dryad Tarindrella back to the glade. While he shares the prominent Staghelm surname with Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, his exact connection to the ruling druid remains unconfirmed. Standing directly outside the entrance to the great bough of Aldrassil, Melithar serves as an early point of contact for night elves emerging into the world. A druid who listens to the whisperings of the forest spirits, he has learned that the mysterious woodland protector Tarindrella has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing that something is amiss, Melithar sends newcomers to seek out the dryad southwest of Aldrassil and learn what business brings her to the grove. Bearing the surname Staghelm inevitably draws attention, as Archdruid Fandral Staghelm currently leads the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus following Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance into the Emerald Dream. However, Melithar makes no outward boast of grand heritage, nor does he actively speak of his lineage. Whether he is a distant kinsman of the Archdruid's venerable family line or merely shares an ancient Kaldorei family name, Melithar remains content fulfilling humble duties at the roots of Aldrassil.

npc:merissa-stilwell.text: Merissa Stilwell. Merissa Stilwell is a young human townsperson residing at Northshire Abbey within Elwynn Forest. Standing near the abbey, she offers a cheerful greeting and a helping hand to the newcomers training in Northshire Valley. Standing at Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell greets the fresh recruits who arrive in Northshire Valley. For wandering novices, she offers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting up and getting oriented. Sharing a surname with notable craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom—such as the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell—she remains a peaceful local face amidst the kingdom's rising tensions.

npc:merrin-rockweaver.text: Merrin Rockweaver. Merrin Rockweaver is a dwarven researcher representing the Explorers' League in the Wetlands. Following a violent raptor infestation that overran Whelgar's Excavation Site, she took refuge alongside Prospector Whelgar on a ridge overlooking the site. Merrin Rockweaver traveled to the Wetlands on behalf of the Ironforge Explorers' League to unearth ancient Titan secrets buried beneath the muck. The expedition ended in disaster when the large bones they unearthed drew raptors to the dig. Vicious prehistoric beasts swarmed the trenches, forcing Merrin and the surviving crew to abandon their equipment, notes, and progress. She is now trapped with the few survivors on a bluff overlooking the overrun ruins. Trapped on the bluff, the survivors refuse to let the expedition become an outright failure. While Ormer Ironbraid plots vengeance against the beasts and Prospector Whelgar seeks the tablet fragments left behind in the raptor-infested trenches, Merrin's thoughts turn to her husband Tarrel, who has not heard from her in weeks. She relies on the scout Longbraid sent to find the team to carry word of their plight back to him.

npc:miles-welsh.text: Miles Welsh. Miles Welsh is a Forsaken priest trainer residing deep within the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff. He offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline to priests traversing the tauren capital. Miles Welsh stands far from the plague-scarred ruins of Lordaeron, making his home in the humid, spirit-laden grotto beneath Thunder Bluff known as the Pools of Vision. As a Forsaken priest, he instructs travelers who channel divine and shadowy energies. His presence in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous diplomatic ties binding the Forsaken to the Horde, sharing sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in the arts of shadow and faith.

npc:milli-featherwhistle.text: Milli Featherwhistle. Milli Featherwhistle is a master gnomish mechanostrider engineer stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Following the fall of Gnomeregan, she meticulously handcrafts and maintains the clockwork mounts favored by her kin. She sells her prized mechanical creations to fellow gnomes and trusted allies of the exiled Gnomeregan survivors. Operating outdoors in the biting chill of Steelgrill's Depot just east of Kharanos, Milli Featherwhistle oversees the supply of clockwork steeds for Gnomeregan's displaced populace. Unlike the biological beasts favored by dwarves and night elves, Milli builds her entire inventory herself, personally calibrating gears, pistons, and balancing gyros to ensure each mechanical bird runs at peak efficiency across the snowy crags of Dun Morogh. Every frame and spring in Milli's workshop is rooted in blueprints originally drafted by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. While Milli has integrated modern performance improvements over the years—streamlining chassis weights and refining exhaust vents—she faithfully adheres to the High Tinker's foundational schematics. Her mechanical wonders prove that even in exile, gnomish technological ambition remains thoroughly unbroken.

npc:milton-sheaf.text: Milton Sheaf. Milton Sheaf is the head librarian of the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. Dedicated to preserving the kingdom's history, he oversees the realm's collection of ancient tomes and historical chronicles. He frequently enlists Alliance travelers to recover lost volumes, track down scattered records, and restore neglected manuscripts. Tucked away in the quiet halls of the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf tends to the collective memory of the kingdom. While the court upstairs bustles with politics, squabbling nobles, and military concerns, Sheaf focuses on the preservation of the written word. He considers maintaining accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms a sacred duty, especially in an era fraught with war, loss, and instability. Preserving the library's collection requires constant effort. Books suffer wear and tear, and valuable records are often scattered across the realm in monastic archives, distant outposts, or forgotten ruins. Milton regularly dispatches adventurers across the land—from Northshire Abbey to the distant northern settlement of Southshore—to retrieve misplaced volumes, investigate ancient texts, and ensure rare manuscripts return safely to the keep's shelves.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-earth.text: Minor Manifestation of Earth. A Minor Manifestation of Earth is a localized elemental spirit bound to sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar. Invisible to ordinary sight, it reveals itself only to fledgling shamans who drink the sacred Earth Sapta, providing the rough quartz required to carve their very first earth totem. The spirits of the earth dwell everywhere beneath the dirt and stone, but communicating with them requires deliberate ritual. At sacred landmarks like Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger in the unseen realm, surrounded by even smaller elemental presences. Only initiates who have drunk the Earth Sapta—a ritual draught brewed by shamanic mentors—can lift the veil between the physical world and the elements. Once acknowledged, the spirit imparts the earth's blessings along with a piece of rough quartz, granting the novice the spiritual focal point needed to fashion an Earth Totem.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-water.text: Minor Manifestation of Water. The Minor Manifestation of Water is an elemental spirit found along North Tide's Run on the coast of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital trial for Horde shamans seeking to commune with and master the element of water. Before this peaceful spirit can be consulted, initiates must first cleanse its corrupted counterpart. Lurking along the mist-shrouded shores of North Tide's Run, west of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, the Minor Manifestation of Water represents an essential rite of passage for developing shamans. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, but they can easily fall victim to malevolent blight. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation of this elemental before the pure Minor Manifestation of Water can reveal itself. Once cleansed, the spirit offers guidance to shamans completing their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

npc:misha.text: Misha. Misha is the loyal bear companion of Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde. She wanders Kalimdor faithfully at the half-ogre beastmaster's side. Misha is a brown bear who walks at the side of the wandering Rexxar, a solitary spirit who trusts beasts more than people. Together they have forged a fierce, protective partnership that has weathered countless wildernesses and bloody battles. Misha is far more than a tame pet; she is a seasoned warrior. She fought alongside Rexxar in the brutal conflict against Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, helping ensure the young Horde's survival. When not in battle, her keen senses and strength serve as an extension of Rexxar's will. Currently, travelers venturing along the long tracks through the Stonetalon Mountains, Desolace, and Feralas can spot Misha padding quietly beside Rexxar. Though fierce enough to tear apart any predator foolish enough to threaten them, she remains Rexxar's steadfast anchor in an otherwise untrustworthy world.

npc:misha-tor-kren.text: Misha Tor'kren. Misha Tor'kren is an orc mother dwelling at the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, southeast of Thunder Ridge. Plagued by anxiety over her missing son Kron, she appeals to passing travelers for aid in discovering his fate. Tucked away near the edge of Thunder Ridge, Misha Tor'kren works her isolated farmstead while enduring a parent's worst fear. Her son Kron ventured west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle, but he never returned. With Durotar's frontier dangers stretching orcish watchtowers thin, Misha is left alone to hope for word of his whereabouts, desperate for anyone willing to search the riverbanks for signs of her boy.

npc:mitsuwa.text: Mitsuwa. Mitsuwa is a Darkspear troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the misty coast of Ashenvale. Deeply troubled by the ambush of his traveling kin, he enlists Horde champions to avenge the fallen and reclaim stolen spiritual talismans. Situated at the remote Zoram'gar Outpost on the strand of the Zoram Strand, Mitsuwa serves the Horde alongside his companion Marukai. When a group of traveling trolls bound for the encampment was ambushed and slaughtered by the aggressive Thistlefur furbolgs of northern Ashenvale, Mitsuwa took the loss as a grievous offense. Driven by duty and anger, he directs able-bodied warriors toward the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen troll charms, ensuring the spirits of his kin are honored and their sacred possessions recovered from the beasts.

npc:monte-gazlowe.text: Monte Gazlowe. Gazlowe is the pragmatic goblin engineer and overseer who established and rules the port town of Ratchet. After serving as the Horde's chief engineer during the founding of Durotar and Orgrimmar, he used his substantial earnings to build a bustling, neutral trading hub for the Steamwheedle Cartel. After securing a handsome payday for his engineering work with the new Horde, Gazlowe invested directly into the barren coastline, founding the port of Ratchet. Operating under the Steamwheedle Cartel, he runs the dockside town as a strictly neutral port where Horde, Alliance, and independent traders can barter freely—provided they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy. Following the Third War, Warchief Thrall hired Gazlowe as Durotar's chief engineer to solve critical infrastructure challenges for the nascent orc capital. Gazlowe took on the perilous job of securing a freshwater supply for Orgrimmar, digging extensive tunnels that inadvertently breached subterranean kobold dens. With the timely assistance of the wandering beastmaster Rexxar, Gazlowe managed to blast the caverns shut and complete his assignments. He remains a favored contractor and friend to Thrall, even dispatching his own foreman, Rezlak, to continue assisting orcish construction efforts across Durotar. Though business in Ratchet is lucrative, Gazlowe faces continuous headaches from maritime competition and thievery. The Southsea Freebooters have established camps along the nearby Merchant Coast, intercepting cargo bound for Ratchet and stealing everything from raw ore to Gazlowe's custom-ordered boots. To protect his bottom line, the port boss frequently hires passing sellswords of any allegiance to clean out pirate encampments, retrieve stolen shipments, and settle scores with dockside troublemakers.

npc:moon-priestess-amara.text: Moon Priestess Amara. Moon Priestess Amara is a night elf priestess stationed along the main road west of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Flanked by loyal huntress guards, she keeps watch over the woodland pathways connecting the heart of the bough to the capital city of Darnassus. Stationed at a quiet wayside post west of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara represents both the spiritual authority of the Sisterhood of Elune and the practical vigilance required to keep Teldrassil's roadways secure. She travels and watches with two huntress companions, Nhemai and Yaeliura. To travelers journeying westward, Amara acts as a guiding hand, directing adventurers along the road toward Darnassus and tasking those with burdened spirits to seek out paths of redemption.

npc:mor-rogal.text: Mor'rogal. Mor'rogal is a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. He serves as an advisor and guide for travelers seeking glory and peril within the rugged subterranean reaches of the crags. Perched within the refuge of Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal takes a keen interest in the deep crevices and caverns that cut through the Stonetalon Mountains. Recognizing that the region's twisting subterranean passes offer both great riches and lethal danger, he directs brave Horde wanderers to investigate troubled areas like the Boulderslide Ravine. For Mor'rogal, delving into these treacherous depths is not merely a matter of survival, but a test of spirit for those who follow their heart and soul in search of glory.

npc:morgan-pestle.text: Morgan Pestle. Morgan Pestle is a human alchemist and shopkeeper who runs Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City. Working closely with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire, he handles supplies and alchemical research for the capital. Operating out of Pestle's Apothecary along the busy thoroughfares of Stormwind's Trade District, Morgan Pestle provides alchemical goods, reagents, and practical remedies to city residents and passing travelers. While his brother William maintains a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Morgan keeps the family trade rooted in the heart of the kingdom's capital, receiving shipments, such as his brother's candles, from the rural heartlands.

npc:mountaineer-barleybrew.text: Mountaineer Barleybrew. Mountaineer Barleybrew is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at the South Gate Outpost in Dun Morogh. Guarding the pass leading eastward toward Loch Modan, he relies on hearty dwarven brews to keep sentries alert in the biting cold. Perched at the South Gate Outpost guarding the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew stands as part of Ironforge's border watch. Like many mountaineers serving in the bitter winds of Dun Morogh, he appreciates the fortifying qualities of fine dwarven drink. Bearing the name of the renowned Barleybrew clan, he helps see to it that shipments of potent Shimmer Stout make their way to fellow watchmen who need warmth and stamina during long shifts along the mountain passes.

npc:mountaineer-kadrell.text: Mountaineer Kadrell. Mountaineer Kadrell is a stalwart dwarven sentry stationed across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Serving as a crucial liaison within the Loch Modan Mountaineers, he coordinates reconnaissance, supply deliveries, and border defense across the region. Standing watch in the bustling settlement of Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell acts as an anchor for dwarven defenses throughout Loch Modan. While outposts on the valley's fringes face relentless pressure from troggs, gnolls, and native beasts, Kadrell remains at the center of town to organize reinforcements, relay orders, and assess incoming field reports from wandering scouts. Kadrell's duties frequently involve maintaining contact between Thelsamar and remote forward positions. Whether coordinating with Mountaineer Stormpike or sending adventurers to report to sentries like Mountaineer Rockgar, Kadrell ensures that the isolated outposts guarding the mountain passes receive vital supplies, reinforcements, and defensive intelligence.

npc:mountaineer-stormpike.text: Mountaineer Stormpike. Mountaineer Stormpike is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at Algaz Station in northern Loch Modan. Watching over the mountain pass leading toward the Wetlands, he works tirelessly to keep vital supply routes safe from lurking troggs and kobolds. As a proud member of the Stormpike clan, his loyalty lies squarely with Ironforge and the safety of dwarven lands. Perched along the northern border of Loch Modan, Algaz Station serves as a critical checkpoint before the perilous descent into the Wetlands. Mountaineer Stormpike is stationed here amid rocky crags and constant wilderness threats. His primary duty is maintaining the line of communication and keeping the roads open for travelers and supply convoys traversing through Dun Algaz. The northern reaches of Loch Modan are plagued by relentless pests, from kobolds infesting nearby digs to subterranean troggs. Stormpike routinely enlists passing adventurers to disrupt these threats, particularly targeting the kobolds who have moved into the Silver Stream Mine and put their filthy paws on the Miners' League's stored dwarven tools.

npc:mountaineer-thalos.text: Mountaineer Thalos. Mountaineer Thalos is a dwarven sentry stationed at the Coldridge Valley mouth of Coldridge Pass. Tasked with guarding the route, he warns travelers about the sudden trogg infestation choking the tunnel. Adventurers carrying urgent reports from the valley rely on him to point the way safely toward Kharanos.
